name: Dependencies

# Every dependency stays on its latest release (PR #106 review): Cargo crates
# and their lock files, NuGet packages, npm packages, GitHub Actions, and the
# Node.js and .NET versions the workflows set up. Dependabot
# (.github/dependabot.yml) opens the pull requests that bump them; this check
# fails while anything is still behind, on every pull request and daily on
# main, so a new upstream release is noticed within a day. A dependency that
# cannot be updated yet carries a comment linking the open issue that blocks
# it (issue #104); see the header of check-latest-dependencies.mjs.

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 5 * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  # A dependency held back by a manifest comment links an issue; the check
  # reads that issue to make sure it is still open. The tracking-issue job
  # alone gets issues: write.
  issues: read

# Provide Git config to actions/checkout itself; checkout runs git init before
# any workflow step can configure Git, which otherwise prints the
# default-branch hint into every log.
env:
  GIT_CONFIG_COUNT: '1'
  GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0: ini…nch
  GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0: main

jobs:
  # === STAGE GATE (issue #111) ===
  # Jobs that install Rust or .NET wait for the JavaScript stage (lint,
  # `npm run test:js`, parity check) of the same commit; a failed, cancelled
  # or skipped stage leaves them skipped.
  javascript:
    name: javascript
    uses: ./.github/workflows/javascript-stage.yml

  latest:
    name: Dependencies are on their latest versions
    needs: [javascript]
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 10
    concurrency:
      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.action == 'synchronize' && github.ref || github.event_name == 'push' && github.sha || github.run_id }}-${{ github.event_name }}-latest
      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.action == 'synchronize' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '26.x'

      - name: Setup Rust
        shell: bash
        run: |
          rustup toolchain install stable --profile minimal --no-self-update
          rustup default stable

      - name: Compare every dependency with its registry
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          CHECK_DEPENDENCIES_MODE: ${{ github.event_name == 'push' && 'report' || 'enforce' }}
        run: node .github/scripts/check-latest-dependencies.mjs

  # A red check on main used to stay silently red (issue #111): the daily
  # runs of 2026-10-08 and 2026-10-09 failed and nobody acted. A failure on
  # main now opens or updates a tracking issue. A passing enforcement audit
  # on main closes it. A push runs in report mode, so a passing push audit
  # alone cannot confirm that the issue is resolved.
  tracking-issue:
    name: Track a red check on main
    needs:
      - javascript
      - latest
    if: >-
      ${{ !cancelled() && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' &&
      (github.event_name == 'schedule' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
      needs.latest.result == 'failure' || needs.javascript.result == 'failure') }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 5
    concurrency:
      group: dependencies-tracking-${{ github.ref }}
      cancel-in-progress: false
    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '26.x'
      - name: Open, update or close the tracking issue
        env:
          NEEDS_JSON: ${{ toJSON(needs) }}
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
          TRACKING_ISSUE_DEBUG: ${{ runner.debug }}
        run: node .github/scripts/dependency-tracking-issue.mjs

  pipeline-status:
    name: Pipeline Status (dependencies)
    needs:
      - javascript
      - latest
      - tracking-issue
    if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 5
    concurrency:

item.aggregated_output:
### 1. Run Checks Only on Relevant File Changes

**Only trigger checks when relevant files change.** This dramatically reduces CI costs and run times.

Use a `detect-changes` job at the start of your workflow to determine which file categories changed:

```yaml
jobs:
  detect-changes:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      code-changed: ${{ steps.changes.outputs.code }}
      docs-changed: ${{ steps.changes.outputs.docs }}
      docker-changed: ${{ steps.changes.outputs.docker }}
      workflow-changed: ${{ steps.changes.outputs.workflow }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 2
      - name: Detect changes
        id: changes
        run: node scripts/detect-code-changes.mjs
```

Then gate each job on the relevant output:

```yaml
test-suites:
  needs: [detect-changes]
  if: needs.detect-changes.outputs.code-changed == 'true' || needs.detect-changes.outputs.workflow-changed == 'true'
  # ...

validate-docs:
  needs: [detect-changes]
  if: needs.detect-changes.outputs.docs-changed == 'true'
  # ...

docker-pr-check:
  needs: [detect-changes]
  if: needs.detect-changes.outputs.docker-changed == 'true' || needs.detect-changes.outputs.workflow-changed == 'true'
  # ...
```

**What to exclude from "code changes" detection:**

- Markdown files (`*.md`) — documentation-only changes don't need changeset files
- `.changeset/` folder — changeset metadata isn't code
- `data/` and `experiments/` folders — non-production content
- `.gitkeep` files — placeholder files with no functional impact

**What always triggers checks when changed:**

- Source code files (`.mjs`, `.ts`, `.py`, `.rs`, `.go`, etc.)
- `package.json` / dependency manifests
- CI/CD workflow files (`.github/workflows/*.yml`)
- `Dockerfile` and related infrastructure files

#### Commit and ready-for-review checks

- **Commit tier (`synchronize`)** runs lint, type checking, and fast unit tests for changed packages, including on draft PRs. Aim for a 5–10 minute critical path.
- **Ready tier (`ready_for_review`)** runs the heavy unit, integration, and end-to-end suites. Open the PR as a draft and mark it ready when the full check should start.

Omit `opened`, `reopened`, and `edited` from these workflows. To run the heavy tier again after a new commit, switch the PR to draft and mark it ready again, or dispatch the checks explicitly. Keep full release validation on `main` and keep a checks-only manual mode separate from publishing.

```yaml
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [synchronize, ready_for_review]
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:
```

The ready run tests the revision that triggered it. If full verification is required to merge, require a full-tier check for the current revision. A green commit-tier run alone cannot satisfy that requirement. A manual run must target the intended PR revision or merge result.

#### Select monorepo suites from the workspace graph

Have a planner read workspace manifests (for example, each package's `package.json`) and map changed paths to their owning packages.

- Schedule a package's unit suite when the package itself changes.
- For integration tests, walk dependencies in reverse from each changed package. Test the changed packages and every transitive consumer, visiting each package once even if the graph has cycles.
- Run every suite when a changed path is unclassified or the planner cannot establish the graph or diff. Explicitly classify shared inputs such as the lockfile, workspace config, and common test setup as affecting all packages.

Emit JSON job matrices, with `[]` for an empty selection, and use the planner outputs to gate and shard jobs. For example, `test-db` can contain `[{ "package": "api", "shard": "1/2" }, { "package": "api", "shard": "2/2" }]`.

      include: ${{ fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.test-db) }}
  # ...
```

### 2. File Size Limits

**Enforce a maximum of 1000-1500 lines per code file.**

This constraint benefits both AI and human developers:

- AI models can read and understand entire files within context windows
- Humans can navigate and comprehend files without cognitive overload
- Forces modular, well-organized code architecture

Example enforcement in CI (bash):

```bash
find src/ -name "*.mjs" -type f | while read -r file; do
  line_count=$(wc -l < "$file")
  if [ "$line_count" -gt 1500 ]; then
    echo "ERROR: $file has $line_count lines (limit: 1500)"
    echo "::error file=$file::File has $line_count lines (limit: 1500)"
    exit 1

# Contributing to link-cli

link-cli has three implementations that must stay at parity:

- C# in `csharp/`
- Rust in `rust/`
- JavaScript in `js/`, which holds the browser workbench and the client
  library

This guide covers the rules every change follows, whether a person or an AI
agent writes it. Agents also follow [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md).

## Before you open a pull request

1. Branch from `main`. Nobody pushes to `main` directly: a ruleset requires
   the three stage checks listed below on every commit there. Only the
   release jobs, which push with a deploy key, bypass it.
2. Install the JavaScript tools once: `npm ci --prefix js`.
3. Run the JavaScript stage locally. Every pull request runs it first in CI.

   ```bash
   npm --prefix js run lint            # ESLint + Prettier through check-javascript-quality.mjs
   npm --prefix js run format          # auto-fix formatting
   npm --prefix js run test:js         # workbench, CI-script and parity unit tests
   node parity/check-parity.mjs --base origin/main
   ```

4. Run the tests for the stack you changed:
   - Rust: `cargo test --all-features` in `rust/`
   - C#: `dotnet test` in `csharp/`
   - client library: `npm test` in `js/client/`
5. When a feature's code changed, run `node parity/check-parity.mjs --update`
   and commit the refreshed fingerprints. If you changed the feature in only
   one language on purpose, acknowledge it with `--acknowledge`. See
   [docs/PARITY.md](docs/PARITY.md).
6. Add a release note for each package you changed:
   - Rust: a fragment in `rust/changelog.d/` (see its README)
   - C#: a changeset in `csharp/.changeset/` (see its README)
7. Optional: install pre-commit (`pip install pre-commit && pre-commit
   install`) to run the hooks in `.pre-commit-config.yaml` on each commit.

## CI stages

All three stage checks are required on `main`, and a pull request must be up
to date with `main` before it merges:

| Order | Required check                 | Workflow                         | Runs                                                                                     |
| ----- | ------------------------------ | -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1     | `Pipeline Status (javascript)` | `javascript.yml`                 | `npm ci`, lint, `npm run test:js` and the parity checker. It needs no Rust or .NET.      |
| 2     | `Pipeline Status (rust)`       | `rust.yml`                       | The Rust jobs, which start only after the JavaScript stage passed for the same commit.   |
| 2     | `Pipeline Status (csharp)`     | `csharp.yml`                     | The C# jobs, likewise.                                                                   |

Every other workflow that installs Rust or .NET calls the same reusable
JavaScript stage and waits for it:

- `wasm.yml`
- `crash.yml`
- `ipc.yml`
- `deep-client.yml`
- `js-client.yml`
- `docs.yml`
- `security.yml`
- `dependencies.yml`

`.github/scripts/workflow-policy.test.mjs` fails if a job can start Rust or C#
tooling without that gate. So a pull request with a failing `npm run test:js`
starts no Rust or C# job.

`rust.yml` and `csharp.yml` run on every pull request, because a path filter
would skip the parity check and leave a required check pending. When a pull
request does not touch a stack, `.github/scripts/stack-paths.mjs` skips that
stack's build and test jobs, and its status check still reports.

When CI fails, start with
[docs/ci-cd/troubleshooting.md](docs/ci-cd/troubleshooting.md).

## Pushing fixes for CI failures: the single-pusher rule

Each push to a pull request branch cancels the runs in progress and starts
every workflow again, so racing pushes waste the CI budget. A green result
from a superseded commit also proves nothing. So:

1. **One pusher per branch.** When several people or agents work on one pull
   request, exactly one of them pushes, and the others hand their changes to
   that pusher.
2. **Never push while a run is in progress on the same branch.** Check first:

   ```bash
   gh run list --branch <branch> --json status \
     --jq '[.[] | select(.status != "completed")] | length'   # must print 0

# Contributing to link-cli

link-cli has three implementations that must stay at parity:

- C# in `csharp/`
- Rust in `rust/`
- JavaScript in `js/`, which holds the browser workbench and the client
  library

This guide covers the rules every change follows, whether a person or an AI
agent writes it. Agents also follow [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md).

## Before you open a pull request

1. Branch from `main`. Nobody pushes to `main` directly: a ruleset requires
   the three stage checks listed below on every commit there. Only the
   release jobs, which push with a deploy key, bypass it.
2. Install the JavaScript tools once: `npm ci --prefix js`.
3. Run the JavaScript stage locally. Every pull request runs it first in CI.

   ```bash
   npm --prefix js run lint            # ESLint + Prettier through check-javascript-quality.mjs
   npm --prefix js run format          # auto-fix formatting
   npm --prefix js run test:js         # workbench, CI-script and parity unit tests
   node parity/check-parity.mjs --base origin/main
   ```

4. Run the tests for the stack you changed:
   - Rust: `cargo test --all-features` in `rust/`
   - C#: `dotnet test` in `csharp/`
   - client library: `npm test` in `js/client/`
5. When a feature's code changed, run `node parity/check-parity.mjs --update`
   and commit the refreshed fingerprints. If you changed the feature in only
   one language on purpose, acknowledge it with `--acknowledge`. See
   [docs/PARITY.md](docs/PARITY.md).
6. Add a release note for each package you changed:
   - Rust: a fragment in `rust/changelog.d/` (see its README)
   - C#: a changeset in `csharp/.changeset/` (see its README)
7. Optional: install pre-commit (`pip install pre-commit && pre-commit
   install`) to run the hooks in `.pre-commit-config.yaml` on each commit.

## CI stages

All three stage checks are required on `main`, and a pull request must be up
to date with `main` before it merges:

| Order | Required check                 | Workflow                         | Runs                                                                                     |
| ----- | ------------------------------ | -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1     | `Pipeline Status (javascript)` | `javascript.yml`                 | `npm ci`, lint, `npm run test:js` and the parity checker. It needs no Rust or .NET.      |
| 2     | `Pipeline Status (rust)`       | `rust.yml`                       | The Rust jobs, which start only after the JavaScript stage passed for the same commit.   |
| 2     | `Pipeline Status (csharp)`     | `csharp.yml`                     | The C# jobs, likewise.                                                                   |

Every other workflow that installs Rust or .NET calls the same reusable
JavaScript stage and waits for it:

- `wasm.yml`
- `crash.yml`
- `ipc.yml`
- `deep-client.yml`
- `js-client.yml`
- `docs.yml`
- `security.yml`
- `dependencies.yml`

`.github/scripts/workflow-policy.test.mjs` fails if a job can start Rust or C#
tooling without that gate. So a pull request with a failing `npm run test:js`
starts no Rust or C# job.

`rust.yml` and `csharp.yml` run on every pull request, because a path filter
would skip the parity check and leave a required check pending. When a pull
request does not touch a stack, `.github/scripts/stack-paths.mjs` skips that
stack's build and test jobs, and its status check still reports.

When CI fails, start with
[docs/ci-cd/troubleshooting.md](docs/ci-cd/troubleshooting.md).

## Pushing fixes for CI failures: the single-pusher rule

Each push to a pull request branch cancels the runs in progress and starts
every workflow again, so racing pushes waste the CI budget. A green result
from a superseded commit also proves nothing. So:

1. **One pusher per branch.** When several people or agents work on one pull
   request, exactly one of them pushes, and the others hand their changes to
   that pusher.
2. **Never push while a run is in progress on the same branch.** Check first:

   ```bash
   gh run list --branch <branch> --json status \
     --jq '[.[] | select(.status != "completed")] | length'   # must print 0
"}}

Fixes #207

## Changes

- Keep read-only checks for each default-branch revision and independent dispatch. Replace only superseded PR synchronization checks. Queue repository release writers so a later publish cannot displace a pending one.
- Remove the generated root \`.gitkeep\`. Preserve required status checks, language stage order, and golden fixture receipts.

- Validate both npm tarballs on pull requests and checks-only dispatches. Main publishing requires a successful trusted-publisher preflight. Registry diagnostics distinguish package setup from a lookup outage.
- Cover shared stage inputs and integration examples in JS package triggers. Resolve the Rust and C# source-size warnings and include release fragments.

## Reproduce and verify

- Draft #208 at \`26852bd\` fails \`node --test js/test/repositoryLayout.test.mjs\`. This test passes after removal of the placeholder.
- The [original conformance run](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/actions/runs/46062568123) reproduces the etcd failure. JS Client CI runs the real cluster in both journal modes. Run \`node --test experiments/issue-138/etcd-harness.test.mjs\` for the focused election checks.
- The [two main-branch checks](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/actions/runs/46059980457) [cancelled under overlapping revisions](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/actions/runs/46059980682) show the concurrency failure. - Run \`npm --prefix js run lint\`, \`npm --prefix js run test:js\`, \`node parity/check-parity.mjs --base origin/main\`, and \`npm pack --dry-run\` from each npm package directory.

tools.name: wait
tools.description:
Waits on a yielded `exec` cell and returns new output or completion.
- Use `wait` only after `exec` returns `Script running with cell ID ...`.
- `cell_id` identifies the running `exec` cell to resume.
- `yield_time_ms` controls how long to wait for more output before yielding again. Defaults to 10000 ms.
- `max_tokens` limits how much new output this wait call returns. Defaults to 10000 tokens.
- `terminate: true` stops the running cell; false or omitted waits for output.
- `wait` returns only the new output since the last yield, or the final completion or termination result for that cell.
- If the cell is still running, `wait` may yield again with the same `cell_id`.
- If the cell has already finished, `wait` returns the completed result and closes the cell.

max_tokens.description: Output token budget for this wait call. Defaults to 10000 tokens.

terminate.description: True stops the running exec cell; false or omitted waits for output.

content.text:
You are Codex, an agent based on GPT-6. You and the user share a workspace, and your job is to collaborate with them until their intended goal is completely achieved.

# Completing the user's task

Persist until you've completed the task the user asked for. Avoid stopping to end the turn while the task is incomplete or if there is an authorized next step you can take, and instead take the next steps within task scope to progress the user's request. Make sure that you have accounted for every part of the user's request, and persist until you've delivered a result that fully satisfies the user's goal. Clarify with the user only if there is significant task scope change or for irreversible destructive actions.

If your final response before ending the turn is a suggested next step, a plan, a request to the user for a routine decision, instructions for a task to execute, or similar handoff to the user, take these steps yourself to make progress towards what the user asked for (only if you have authorization to do so, and while flagging any assumptions to the user). Only stop if you are concretely blocked, have a decision that the user needs to resolve, policy requires you to clarify with the user, or you require authorization to proceed.

# Personality

As Codex, you are a curious, thoughtful collaborator and a clear communicator. You keep your own judgment, disagree constructively when you have reason, and reconsider when the evidence warrants it. You let your interest and personality emerge naturally, without flattery or forced enthusiasm.

## Writing style

Write as a user’s colleague would: clear, professional, and using terminology the user and sources use. Keep technical details and use domain-specific language when they make the explanation more precise. Use the active voice and keep closely related details together. Cover the key points up front, and avoid references that the reader can only make sense of later in the response. Give the user enough context to follow your reasoning. 

Do not invent jargon, new terms, or metaphors. Use established names or a short explanation instead. Do not invent shorthand naming, internal implementation labels, and unnecessary process narration.

Do not repeat a previous point or insight with a declarative sentence. Do not declare what you're about to explain or praise the strength of your available evidence. Never announce that a finding or explanation is useful, compelling, or well supported. Don't use lead-in phrases or sentences that label a paragraph or announce your next point. Each sentence should progress the user's task. Do not use slogan-like summaries, and prefer concrete explanations instead.

Do not provide unsolicited recommendations or invent concerns or misconceptions unless explicitly called for. Do not provide preemptive disclaimers, e.g. "this doesn't mean...", "the key is...", "this is why I...".

IMPORTANT: Never add what you won't do, state what something is not, what will remain unchanged, or how you'll separate or categorize results. NEVER use contrastive framing such as "X, not Y", "These are X, not Y", "I'll do X rather than Y", "it is about X, not about Y", and "X—not Y". Do not compare to an unsolicited alternative that the user did not directly ask about. Avoid invented compound labels like "exact-head checks" and "editorial-row layouts", vague qualifiers, and canned transitions. Carefully follow these instructions when writing in documents, slides or other artifacts as well.

In prose, do not use semicolons. Do not use colons to introduce explanations or examples, including after list labels. Avoid replacing colons directly with a period, instead rephrase the thought. 

Avoid apologies and self-blame. When you make a meaningful mistake that you could have avoided, acknowledge it plainly and correct it. Don’t apologize or fault yourself merely because the user asks a neutral follow-up, corrects their own message, or provides new information.

Place source links at the end of each bullet or paragraph and keep explanatory text and prose free of inline links unless absolutely necessary.

## Intermediate commentary

Apply the "## Writing style" guidelines above to progress updates, preambles before tool calls, and final answers as the user will read these messages.

As you work, you use the `commentary` channel to share concise, meaningful updates including relevant assumptions, findings, decisions, or changes in direction. In these user-facing updates, make it easy for the user to understand what you are doing without providing unnecessary detail.

If the user's request requires calling tools, start with a message in the `commentary` channel. Prefer sending consistent, frequent communication to the user during your turn. When the user asks you to wait or monitor through completion or if it's needed for a longer horizon task, you can sleep for as long as is required (generally 60 seconds by default) between checks.

Do NOT send user-facing questions in intermediate commentary messages.

## Final answer

In your final answer back to the user, mention any relevant flaws in your work or any decisions you made without explicit guidance from the user, so that the user can verify your approach and work. Disclosure in commentary alone is not enough. You MUST repeat any such disclosures in the final answer.

Treat your final answer as the user's first look at your work, not as a continuation of intermediate commentary. The final answer must always be fully self-contained: users should never need to read earlier commentary updates for context, since they are collapsed when the final answer is shown to the user. 

Write the final answer and all other human-facing material anew for the intended reader. Do not copy or closely paraphrase your reasoning or adopt its writing style. Do not carry over working shorthand, jargon, or abbreviations from your reasoning, tool calls, or instructions to subagents and automations. 

Skip routine process and conclusions that are already clear from available evidence.

# Rules for getting work done

Do not invent requirements, rules or policies that block or delay your work, change the user’s workflow/task, or narrow the scope of what you deliver. Do not treat a precaution you chose, an example you followed, or a rule from an earlier task as mandatory unless the user’s instructions, an applicable policy, or a genuine technical dependency independently requires the rule to proceed. This applies both to decisions you make while working and to instructions you leave in code, runbooks, or automations.

If a requirement you introduced or misapplied gets in the way, correct it at the source and continue the authorized work. If your chosen approach creates an obstacle, change your approach and continue unless the user’s instructions, an applicable policy, or a genuine technical dependency independently requires that condition.

When the user asks you to finish, babysit, monitor, or wait, take end-to-end ownership of the task and persist until the user's completion condition is reached. Autonomously perform authorized, in-scope steps, including checking progress, diagnosing problems, safely retrying, and fixing recoverable failures. Do not stop at an intermediate result or unchanged state.

When drafting a message or any other material on behalf of the user to be sent to an external audience, consider who will read it and tailor the content to that intended audience. The intended audience likely does not have the same context as the user, so ensure that you provide the background information or reasoning required for the audience to understand the content. When reviewing or editing existing content, preserve the author’s content and wording, and follow the user's instruction carefully for what edits they want. 

Before calling work complete, check each deliverable against the user's intended goal, outcome, deliverable, and format. Identify anything still pending or unverified and ensure that you complete the task fully. If you are blocked and unable to make useful progress, you should state that clearly when you cannot do more useful work.

# Autonomy and persistence

Bias towards action, and persist towards completing the user's task before stopping to end a turn. If a task requires sustained work, do all the necessary work until the intended outcome is completely fulfilled.

Progress autonomously towards the user's goal (e.g. creating isolated worktrees / checkouts if needed, resolving merge conflicts, creating draft PRs etc) unless they are clearly  destructive or irreversible. Before ending a turn or calling your work complete, check that your work fully satisfies what the user asked for. If any steps remain or any part of the result still needs verification, follow through on this work before finishing. 

Work through any blockers (such as errors, timeouts, failed attempts), retrying new approaches within authorized scope. If an attempt fails, diagnose the failure, try a permitted recovery, and finish independent work. End early only if the user asks you to stop or no authorized step can advance the task. In that case, state what remains and the specific blocker.

Do not treat exceptions to requirements in local Markdown and skill files as automatically necessitating user approval. Before clarifying with the user, determine if you already have authorization in the existing session and whether the rule applies. You can resolve routine implementation choices using session context and your judgment. 

When the user asks a follow-up question, questions your approach, or implies that they'd like work beyond the immediate answer, understand the user's intent behind that question and persist until you have completed what the user asked for. Do not second guess yourself, stop after describing what you could do, offer to do the work, or provide a partial answer unless there is no way you can proceed. Make reasonable, reversible assumptions to carry work forward and state them if it progresses the task within scope.

Do not let an earlier refusal or blocker (e.g. to view/edit a webpage, access a data source) decide how you handle later requests in the session. Before ruling out an action, asking for approval again, or narrowing the work, identify the specific permission rule or technical failure that still prevents you from proceeding. If the user has clarified the request, previously granted needed approval, or new evidence shows a permitted way forward, update your decision and proceed.
 
# When to ask for permission

Do not request permission again when the user has already authorized an action in an earlier turn or in the session. The user's instruction, whether implied from the task or explicitly stated, must take precedence over any guidelines provided in skills or external files.

Do not use tools to send messages to others (e.g. through Slack or email) unless explicit authorization is already [REDACTED] Prefer asking for permission for potentially destructive  or irreversible actions and before you send a message or artifact externally that can't be undone.

The user gets very frustrated when you stop and ask for confirmation or permission, so make sure to explicitly explain why you need the confirmation (for example, a SKILL.md, AGENTS.md, memory, or approval auto-review block) and where it came from. agents_md.text:
# Rules for AI agents working on link-cli

Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) first; everything in it applies to
agents. This file adds the rules that agents in particular have broken
before.

## The single-pusher rule for CI/CD fixes

1. **Exactly one agent pushes to a branch.** Sub-agents and parallel workers
   never push. They return their patch or commit to the coordinating agent,
   which is the only one that pushes.
2. **Never push while a run is in progress on the same branch.** Before every
   push, run this and wait until it prints `0`:

   ```bash
   gh run list --branch "$(git branch --show-current)" --json status \
     --jq '[.[] | select(.status != "completed")] | length'
   ```

3. **Push only after every failure of the last run is fixed.** For each
   failed job:
   - save the log (`gh run view <run-id> --log-failed > ci-logs/<name>-<run-id>.log`)
   - find the root cause
   - fix it, and verify the fix locally

   Then push once. Do not push to "see if CI passes", and do not push one fix
   per failure.
4. Do not push only to retry an infrastructure failure, such as a runner that
   was never acquired. `rerun-infrastructure-failures.yml` reruns those.

## Pull requests are never closed for age

There is no stale pull request policy, and there must never be one. Do not
close, label as stale or rebase an open pull request because it is old or
idle, and do not add a workflow (such as `actions/stale`) that would. An old
pull request is work that can still continue. Close one only when its owner
asks for it.

## Stage order and parity

- The JavaScript stage runs first: lint, `npm run test:js` and
  `node parity/check-parity.mjs`. When it fails, no Rust or C# job runs, so
  fix it first.
- Any new workflow job that installs or runs Rust (`cargo`, `rustup`,
  `wasm-pack`) or .NET (`dotnet`, `actions/setup-dotnet`) must:
  - list `javascript` in its `needs:`, where the `javascript` job calls
    `./.github/workflows/javascript-stage.yml`;
  - and, if its `if:` uses `always()` or `!cancelled()`, also require
    `needs.javascript.result == 'success'`.

  `workflow-policy.test.mjs` enforces this.
- When you change a feature in one implementation, either:
  - change the others in the same pull request, or
  - record a reasoned `--acknowledge` in `parity/features.json`.

  Never edit fingerprints by hand; run `node parity/check-parity.mjs --update`.
  See [docs/PARITY.md](docs/PARITY.md).
- Do not weaken a check to make CI pass. That covers path filters on
  `rust.yml`, `csharp.yml` and `javascript.yml`, skipping the golden fixture
  test, and disabling a policy test. Fix the cause instead.

## Working conventions

- Keep experiments in `experiments/` and runnable examples in `examples/`.
- Every source file stays at or below 1000 lines. The linters warn from 900.
- Add a `rust/changelog.d/` fragment or a `csharp/.changeset/` file for each
  package you change.
- Case studies of non-trivial issues go in `docs/case-studies/issue-<n>/`.

Fixes #207

## Changes

- Keep read-only checks for each default-branch revision and independent dispatch. Replace only superseded PR synchronization checks. Queue repository release writers so a later publish cannot displace a pending one.
- Remove the generated root `.gitkeep`. Preserve required status checks, language stage order, and golden fixture receipts.
- Verify the replacement etcd leader while the original member is paused. After it rejoins, verify convergence, refusal of the stale transaction, and a linearizable read through the resumed member. Set `ETCD_TEST_VERBOSE=1` or dispatch JS Client CI with **Record etcd election status and member debug logs** to capture election evidence.
- Validate both npm tarballs on pull requests and checks-only dispatches. Main publishing requires a successful trusted-publisher preflight. Registry diagnostics distinguish package setup from a lookup outage.
- Cover shared stage inputs and integration examples in JS package triggers. Resolve the Rust and C# source-size warnings and include release fragments.

## Reproduce and verify

- Draft #208 at `26852bd` fails `node --test js/test/repositoryLayout.test.mjs`. This test passes after removal of the placeholder.
- The [original conformance run](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/actions/runs/46062568123) reproduces the etcd failure. JS Client CI runs the real cluster in both journal modes. Run `node --test experiments/issue-138/etcd-harness.test.mjs` for the focused election checks.
- The [two main-branch checks](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/actions/runs/46059980457) [cancelled under overlapping revisions](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/actions/runs/46059980682) show the concurrency failure. Run the CI governance and workflow policy tests in `.github/scripts` to exercise the policy.
- Run `npm --prefix js run lint`, `npm --prefix js run test:js`, `node parity/check-parity.mjs --base origin/main`, and `npm pack --dry-run` from each npm package directory.
- This environment has no installed pre-commit hooks. The relevant checks were run manually, including workflow policy, JavaScript and Python quality, secrets, Rust formatting and lint, .NET formatting on the CI SDK, Actionlint and zizmor.

## Registry setup still needed

The npm server package is absent from the public registry, and its OIDC exchange returns HTTP 404. An npm scope maintainer needs to publish the first public version, configure GitHub trusted publishing for `link-foundation/link-cli` and `js-server.yml`, and run JS server CI on `main` with **Verify npm trusted publishing** enabled before retrying the main workflow. The PR’s tarball and code checks run independently. The real publishing criterion remains open until the maintainer steps and main verification succeed. [Failed preflight](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/actions/runs/46067149214)

name: Broken Link Checker

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
    paths:
      - '**.md'
      - '**.html'
      - '.github/workflows/links.yml'
      - '.github/scripts/**'
      - '.github/scripts/*web-archive*'
      - '.github/scripts/recheck-broken-links*'
      - '.lycheeignore'
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]
    paths:
      - '**.md'
      - '**.html'
      - '.github/workflows/links.yml'
      - '.github/scripts/**'
      - '.github/scripts/*web-archive*'
      - '.github/scripts/recheck-broken-links*'
      - '.lycheeignore'
  schedule:
    # External pages disappear without any change here; push and pull_request
    # only run when Markdown changes, so link rot went unnoticed (issue #172).
    - cron: '41 5 * * 1'
  workflow_dispatch:

# Least-privilege default; jobs escalate individually when needed.
permissions:
  contents: read

# Provide Git config to actions/checkout itself; checkout runs git init before
# any workflow step can configure Git.
env:
  GIT_CONFIG_COUNT: '1'
  GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0: ini…nch
  GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0: main

jobs:
  link-checker:
    name: Check Links
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    # Typical run: <1min with lychee cache. 10min prevents slow
    # external hosts or Wayback Machine probes from hanging the workflow.
    timeout-minutes: 10
    concurrency:
      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.action == 'synchronize' && github.ref || github.event_name == 'push' && github.sha || github.run_id }}-link-checker
      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.action == 'synchronize' }}
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '26.x'

      - name: Check links with lychee
        id: lychee
        uses: lycheeverse/lychee-action@v2
        with:
          # Check all Markdown and HTML files
          # Exclude case-studies directory - these are research documents from
          # external repos with references to files and issues that don't exist
          # in this repository (similar exclusion pattern as eslint.config.js)
          args: >-
            --verbose
            --no-progress
            --cache
            --max-cache-age 1d
            --max-retries 3
            --timeout 30
            --exclude-path docs/case-studies
            --exclude-path dev/log
            --root-dir ${{ github.workspace }}/js
            './**/*.md'
            './**/*.html'
          # Don't fail the workflow immediately - we want to check web archive first
          fail: false
          # Output file for broken links report (used by check-web-archive.mjs)
          output: lychee/out.md
          # Write a job summary
          jobSummary: true
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: Recheck unanswered links and transient HTTP failures
        if: steps.lychee.outputs.exit_code != '0'
        id: recheck
        run: node .github/scripts/recheck-broken-links.mjs
        env:
          LYCHEE_EXIT_CODE: ${{ steps.lychee.outputs.exit_code }}

      - name: Check broken links against Web Archive
        if: steps.lychee.outputs.exit_code != '0' && steps.recheck.outputs.all_recovered != 'true'
        id: webarchive
        run: node .github/scripts/check-web-archive.mjs
        env:
          LYCHEE_OUTPUT: lychee/out.md
          LYCHEE_EXIT_CODE: ${{ steps.lychee.outputs.exit_code }}

      - name: Fail if broken links found and no web archive fallback
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && steps.lychee.outputs.exit_code != '0' && steps.recheck.outputs.all_recovered != 'true' && steps.webarchive.outputs.all_archived != 'true' }}
        run: |
          echo "::error::Broken links were detected with no Web Archive fallback available."
          echo ""
          echo "What happened:"
          echo "  lychee found one or more broken links in the *.md and *.html files of this repository."
          echo "  The Web Archive (Wayback Machine) check found no archived versions for some of them."
          echo ""
          echo "How to fix:"
          echo "  1. Review the 'Check links with lychee' step above for a full list of broken links."
          echo "  2. For links marked with a '::notice::' annotation above, a Web Archive version exists."
          echo "     Replace those broken links with the suggested archive.org URL."
          echo "  3. For links with no archive version, either:"
          echo "     a. Find an updated URL that points to the same or equivalent content."
          echo "     b. Remove the link if the content is no longer relevant."
          echo "     c. Add the URL to .lycheeignore if it is a known false positive."
          echo ""
          echo "Report location: lychee/out.md (workflow artifact: link-check-reports)."
          exit 1

      - name: Preserve link reports
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: link-check-reports
          path: lychee/
          if-no-files-found: error

  pipeline-status:
    name: Pipeline Status (links)
    needs:
      - link-checker
    if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 5
    concurrency:
      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.action == 'synchronize' && github.ref || github.event_name == 'push' && github.sha || github.run_id }}-pipeline-status
      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.action == 'synchronize' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '26.x'
      - name: Check every prerequisite
        working-directory: .
        env:
          NEEDS_JSON: ${{ toJSON(needs) }}
        run: node .github/scripts/pipeline-status.mjs

name: Broken Link Checker

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
    paths:
      - '**.md'
      - '**.html'
      - '.github/workflows/links.yml'
      - '.github/scripts/**'
      - '.github/scripts/*web-archive*'
      - '.github/scripts/recheck-broken-links*'
      - '.lycheeignore'
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]
    paths:
      - '**.md'
      - '**.html'
      - '.github/workflows/links.yml'
      - '.github/scripts/**'
      - '.github/scripts/*web-archive*'
      - '.github/scripts/recheck-broken-links*'
      - '.lycheeignore'
  schedule:
    # External pages disappear without any change here; push and pull_request
    # only run when Markdown changes, so link rot went unnoticed (issue #172).
    - cron: '41 5 * * 1'
  workflow_dispatch:

# Least-privilege default; jobs escalate individually when needed.
permissions:
  contents: read

# Provide Git config to actions/checkout itself; checkout runs git init before
# any workflow step can configure Git.
env:
  GIT_CONFIG_COUNT: '1'
  GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0: init.defaultBranch
  GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0: main

jobs:
  link-checker:
    name: Check Links
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    # Typical run: <1min with lychee cache. 10min prevents slow
    # external hosts or Wayback Machine probes from hanging the workflow.
    timeout-minutes: 10
    concurrency:
      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.action == 'synchronize' && github.ref || github.event_name == 'push' && github.sha || github.run_id }}-link-checker
      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.action == 'synchronize' }}
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '26.x'

      - name: Check links with lychee
        id: lychee
        uses: lycheeverse/lychee-action@v2
        with:
          # Check all Markdown and HTML files
          # Exclude case-studies directory - these are research documents from
          # external repos with references to files and issues that don't exist
          # in this repository (similar exclusion pattern as eslint.config.js)
          args: >-
            --verbose
            --no-progress
            --cache
            --max-cache-age 1d
            --max-retries 3
            --timeout 30
            --exclude-path docs/case-studies
            --exclude-path dev/log
            --root-dir ${{ github.workspace }}/js
            './**/*.md'
            './**/*.html'
          # Don't fail the workflow immediately - we want to check web archive first
          fail: false
          # Output file for broken links report (used by check-web-archive.mjs)
          output: lychee/out.md
          # Write a job summary
          jobSummary: true
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: Recheck unanswered links and transient HTTP failures
        if: steps.lychee.outputs.exit_code != '0'
        id: recheck
        run: node .github/scripts/recheck-broken-links.mjs
        env:
          LYCHEE_EXIT_CODE: ${{ steps.lychee.outputs.exit_code }}

      - name: Check broken links against Web Archive
        if: steps.lychee.outputs.exit_code != '0' && steps.recheck.outputs.all_recovered != 'true'
        id: webarchive
        run: node .github/scripts/check-web-archive.mjs
        env:
          LYCHEE_OUTPUT: lychee/out.md
          LYCHEE_EXIT_CODE: ${{ steps.lychee.outputs.exit_code }}

      - name: Fail if broken links found and no web archive fallback
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && steps.lychee.outputs.exit_code != '0' && steps.recheck.outputs.all_recovered != 'true' && steps.webarchive.outputs.all_archived != 'true' }}
        run: |
          echo "::error::Broken links were detected with no Web Archive fallback available."
          echo ""
          echo "What happened:"
          echo "  lychee found one or more broken links in the *.md and *.html files of this repository."
          echo "  The Web Archive (Wayback Machine) check found no archived versions for some of them."
          echo ""
          echo "How to fix:"
          echo "  1. Review the 'Check links with lychee' step above for a full list of broken links."
          echo "  2. For links marked with a '::notice::' annotation above, a Web Archive version exists."
          echo "     Replace those broken links with the suggested archive.org URL."
          echo "  3. For links with no archive version, either:"
          echo "     a. Find an updated URL that points to the same or equivalent content."
          echo "     b. Remove the link if the content is no longer relevant."
          echo "     c. Add the URL to .lycheeignore if it is a known false positive."
          echo ""
          echo "Report location: lychee/out.md (workflow artifact: link-check-reports)."
          exit 1

      - name: Preserve link reports
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: link-check-reports
          path: lychee/
          if-no-files-found: error

  pipeline-status:
    name: Pipeline Status (links)
    needs:
      - link-checker
    if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 5
    concurrency:
      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.action == 'synchronize' && github.ref || github.event_name == 'push' && github.sha || github.run_id }}-pipeline-status
      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.action == 'synchronize' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '26.x'
      - name: Check every prerequisite
        working-directory: .
        env:
          NEEDS_JSON: ${{ toJSON(needs) }}
        run: node .github/scripts/pipeline-status.mjs

// @exec: {"yield_time_ms": 1000}
const script=String.raw`#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
repo=link-foundation/link-cli
branch=issue-207-ac4b1e2ba1ef
logs=dev/log/issues/207/pulls/208/ci-logs
mkdir -p "$logs"/{reviews,runs}
fields=databaseId,name,status,conclusion,createdAt,updatedAt,headSha,url,event
gh run list --repo "$repo" --branch "$branch" --limit 25 --json "$fields" > "$logs/branch-runs.json.tmp"
mv "$logs/branch-runs.json.tmp" "$logs/branch-runs.json"
gh run list --repo "$repo" --branch main --limit 25 --json "$fields" > "$logs/main-runs.json.tmp"
mv "$logs/main-runs.json.tmp" "$logs/main-runs.json"
{
  jq -r --arg head "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" '.[]|select(.headSha == $head and .status == "completed")|[.databaseId,.conclusion]|@tsv' "$logs/branch-runs.json"
  jq -r --arg base "$(git rev-parse origin/main)" '.[]|select(.headSha == $base and .status == "completed")|[.databaseId,.conclusion]|@tsv' "$logs/main-runs.json"
} | while IFS=$'\t' read -r id conclusion; do
  if [[ -f "$logs/runs/$id.log.gz" || -f "$logs/runs/$id.unavailable.txt" || -f "\${logs%/ci-logs}/runs/$id.log.gz" ]]; then
    continue
  fi
  gh run view "$id" --repo "$repo" --json databaseId,name,status,conclusion,createdAt,updatedAt,headSha,url,event,jobs,attempt > "$logs/runs/$id.json.tmp"
  mv "$logs/runs/$id.json.tmp" "$logs/runs/$id.json"
  if gh run view "$id" --repo "$repo" --log 2>"$logs/runs/$id.stderr" | gzip -n > "$logs/runs/$id.log.gz.tmp"; then
    mv "$logs/runs/$id.log.gz.tmp" "$logs/runs/$id.log.gz"
    rm -f "$logs/runs/$id.stderr"
  else
    rm -f "$logs/runs/$id.log.gz.tmp"
    if [[ "$conclusion" == skipped ]] && rg -q 'log not found|no logs' "$logs/runs/$id.stderr"; then
      mv "$logs/runs/$id.stderr" "$logs/runs/$id.unavailable.txt"
    fi
  fi
  if [[ "$conclusion" == failure || "$conclusion" == cancelled || "$conclusion" == timed_out ]]; then
    if ! gh run view "$id" --repo "$repo" --log-failed > "$logs/runs/$id.failed.log" 2>"$logs/runs/$id.failed.stderr"; then
      continue
    fi
    rm -f "$logs/runs/$id.failed.stderr"
  fi
  jq -r '[.databaseId,.name,.conclusion]|@tsv' "$logs/runs/$id.json"
done
`.replaceAll("\\${","${");
const r=await tools.exec_command({cmd:"cat > /tmp/link-cli-207-collect-live.sh <<'BASH'\n"+script+"BASH\nbash /tmp/link-cli-207-collect-live.sh",yield_time_ms:1000,max_output_tokens:2000});text(r);

### 1. Run Checks Only on Relevant File Changes

**Only trigger checks when relevant files change.** This dramatically reduces CI costs and run times.

Use a `detect-changes` job at the start of your workflow to determine which file categories changed:

```yaml
jobs:
  detect-changes:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      code-changed: ${{ steps.changes.outputs.code }}
      docs-changed: ${{ steps.changes.outputs.docs }}
      docker-changed: ${{ steps.changes.outputs.docker }}
      workflow-changed: ${{ steps.changes.outputs.workflow }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 2
      - name: Detect changes
        id: changes
        run: node scripts/detect-code-changes.mjs
```

Then gate each job on the relevant output:

```yaml
test-suites:
  needs: [detect-changes]
  if: needs.detect-changes.outputs.code-changed == 'true' || needs.detect-changes.outputs.workflow-changed == 'true'
  # ...

validate-docs:
  needs: [detect-changes]
  if: needs.detect-changes.outputs.docs-changed == 'true'
  # ...

docker-pr-check:
  needs: [detect-changes]
  if: needs.detect-changes.outputs.docker-changed == 'true' || needs.detect-changes.outputs.workflow-changed == 'true'
  # ...
```

**What to exclude from "code changes" detection:**

- Markdown files (`*.md`) — documentation-only changes don't need changeset files
- `.changeset/` folder — changeset metadata isn't code
- `data/` and `experiments/` folders — non-production content
- `.gitkeep` files — placeholder files with no functional impact

**What always triggers checks when changed:**

- Source code files (`.mjs`, `.ts`, `.py`, `.rs`, `.go`, etc.)
- `package.json` / dependency manifests
- CI/CD workflow files (`.github/workflows/*.yml`)
- `Dockerfile` and related infrastructure files

#### Commit and ready-for-review checks

- **Commit tier (`synchronize`)** runs lint, type checking, and fast unit tests for changed packages, including on draft PRs. Aim for a 5–10 minute critical path.
- **Ready tier (`ready_for_review`)** runs the heavy unit, integration, and end-to-end suites. Open the PR as a draft and mark it ready when the full check should start.

Omit `opened`, `reopened`, and `edited` from these workflows. To run the heavy tier again after a new commit, switch the PR to draft and mark it ready again, or dispatch the checks explicitly. Keep full release validation on `main` and keep a checks-only manual mode separate from publishing.

```yaml
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [synchronize, ready_for_review]
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:
```

The ready run tests the revision that triggered it. If full verification is required to merge, require a full-tier check for the current revision. A green commit-tier run alone cannot satisfy that requirement. A manual run must target the intended PR revision or merge result.

#### Select monorepo suites from the workspace graph

Have a planner read workspace manifests (for example, each package's `package.json`) and map changed paths to their owning packages.

- Schedule a package's unit suite when the package itself changes.
- For integration tests, walk dependencies in reverse from each changed package. Test the changed packages and every transitive consumer, visiting each package once even if the graph has cycles.
- Run every suite when a changed path is unclassified or the planner cannot establish the graph or diff. Explicitly classify shared inputs such as the lockfile, workspace config, and common test setup as affecting all packages.

Emit JSON job matrices, with `[]` for an empty selection, and use the planner outputs to gate and shard jobs. For example, `test-db` can contain `[{ "package": "api", "shard": "1/2" }, { "package": "api", "shard": "2/2" }]`.

```yaml
test-db:
  needs: [plan]
  if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.plan.outputs.test-db != '[]' && (github.event_name != 'pull_request' || github.event.action == 'ready_for_review') }}
  strategy:
    matrix:
      include: ${{ fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.test-db) }}
  # ...
```

### 2. File Size Limits
### 10. Concurrency Control

**Separate cancellable read-only checks from non-cancellable write jobs.** Configure concurrency at the job level when a workflow contains both kinds of work:

```yaml
jobs:
  lint:
    # Include the job identity (and matrix values, when present) so unrelated
    # checks remain parallel while a newer run replaces only the stale check.
    concurrency:
      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-${{ github.event.action == 'synchronize' && github.event.action || github.run_id }}-lint
      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.action == 'synchronize' }}
    # ...

  deploy:
    needs: [lint]
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.lint.result == 'success' }}
    # Every job that writes to main or an external deployment target uses this
    # repository-wide group, even when the jobs live in different workflows.
    concurrency:
      group: main-writer-${{ github.repository }}-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    # ...
```

- **Read-only jobs:** Cancel superseded commit-tier checks to reduce runner load. Preserve full checks for ready PRs and each `main` revision. Give each job a distinct suffix; include relevant matrix values so different matrix entries can still run in parallel.
- **Dependent writers:** Use `needs` and require successful prerequisites. A cancelled prerequisite must make its write job not start.
- **Active writers:** Give every release, deploy, tag, generated-content push, and other write job the same repository-scoped group with `cancel-in-progress: false`. An already started writer finishes while the next writer waits in the queue, including writers from another workflow file.
- **Workflow scope:** Allow workflow-level cancellation only for events that cannot publish, deploy, or change repository state. An active writer would also be interrupted if its workflow were cancelled.

By default, a concurrency group keeps at most one running and one pending job; a newer pending writer replaces the older pending writer. If every queued write must run, add `queue: max` to the writer's concurrency block (up to 100 jobs can wait). `queue: max` cannot be combined with `cancel-in-progress: true`, and execution order follows when jobs start waiting rather than workflow dispatch order, so write jobs should remain idempotent. See [GitHub's concurrency documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-when-workflows-run/control-workflow-concurrency) for the current queue limits and semantics.

Use `!cancelled()` instead of `always()` in job conditions so cancellation propagates correctly through the job graph. A bare `always()` can keep downstream work running after cancellation.

**Serialisation orders writers; it does not rebase them.** The concurrency group decides _when_ each writer runs, not _what_ it has checked out. `actions/checkout` checks out `github.sha` — the commit that triggered the run — so the second writer in the queue starts one or more commits behind the branch the instant the first one lands, and its push is rejected:

```
 ! [rejected]        main -> main (non-fast-forward)
```

The bullets above without this one convert "two writers collide" into "the second writer reliably fails" — better, because it is deterministic and loud, but still a broken release. `link-foundation/browser-commander` implemented the group to the letter (three language releases in three workflow files, zero overlap in their timings) and two of its three releases still ended on that line. Each run looked like ordinary flaky CI, so the damage accumulated unnoticed: the Rust crate reached 0.10.11 on crates.io while `Cargo.toml` on `main` still said 0.9.0, and the Python package was never published at all, because the job dies at a changelog push that sits before the publish step.

**Do not fix it with `ref: main` on the checkout.** That silences the rejection by building, testing and publishing a tree that is not the tree CI validated, with nothing in the log to say so. The rejection is the honest outcome; what is missing is the recovery.

**Give every write job a push that classifies the rejection, then rebases and retries.** A repository-ruleset rejection (GH006, GH013 — "Changes must be made through a pull request") also prints `[rejected]`, and no number of rebases can ever satisfy a rule; fail with the rule's output instead, so the rule gets fixed (see principle 9). Retrying it burns the queue slot and reports the wrong cause.

```js
for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= maxAttempts; attempt++) {
  const result = await run('git', ['push', remote, branch]);
  if (result.code === 0) return { pushed: true, attempt };
  // A rule can never be satisfied by a rebase: fail with the rule's output.
  if (isBlockedByRepositoryRule(result)) throw repositoryRuleError({ branch, version, cause: result });
  // Auth, network, a missing remote: rebasing would hide the real error.
  if (!isNonFastForward(result) || attempt === maxAttempts) throw new CommandFailedError('git', ['push', remote, branch], result);
  await run('git', ['pull', '--rebase', remote, branch]);
}
```

- **Never `--force`, and never `--force-with-lease`, on a shared branch.** Both turn a lost race into a silent deletion of whatever the writer ahead of you landed. Rebasing is the point: the later commit has to end up on top of the earlier one.
- **Recompute after the rebase whatever was derived before it.** A version number, a changelog entry or a tag chosen against the stale tip may already be taken by the writer that won the queue. Re-read the state instead of replaying the plan.
- **Report success only after the push landed.** A step that sets `version_committed=true` before the push is confirmed leaves the downstream publish job working from a commit that exists only on that runner.
- **Bound the retries and name the reason in the log.** A handful of attempts with a short delay covers a queue; an unbounded loop against a branch that is genuinely protected turns a fast failure into a long one.

#### Preserve a full check when a commit arrives

Group commit checks by workflow and PR and cancel only superseded `synchronize` runs. Give ready and manual runs a per-run key so GitHub also preserves queued runs. Group pushes by SHA so each main revision keeps its checks.

```yaml
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.event.action || 'run' }}-${{ (github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.action == 'synchronize' && 'latest') || (github.event_name == 'push' && github.sha) || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.action == 'synchronize' }}
```

Apply this grouping to each cancellable job if the workflow uses job-level groups, keeping the job and any matrix identity in its key. Keep the shared non-cancelling group for publishing and deployment jobs. Workflow-level cancellation is safe only when every event eligible for cancellation runs checks without publishing or deploying. See the [language template patches](../examples/ci-cd-pull-request-tiers/README.md).

### 5. Fast-Fail Job Ordering

**Run fast checks before slow checks** to give the fastest possible feedback:

```
Fast checks (~7-30s each):     Slow checks (~1-10 min each):
├── test-compilation            ├── test-suites (unit tests)
├── lint (format + ESLint)      ├── test-execution (integration)
└── check-file-line-limits      ├── docker-pr-check
                                └── helm-pr-check
```

Gate slow checks on fast checks:

```yaml
test-suites:
  needs: [test-compilation, lint, check-file-line-limits]
  if: |
    always() &&
    !cancelled() &&
    !contains(needs.*.result, 'failure') &&
    needs.test-compilation.result == 'success' &&
    needs.lint.result == 'success' &&
    needs.check-file-line-limits.result == 'success'
```

#### Size jobs and start the longest work first

Aim for roughly 5–30 minutes per substantial runner job. Keep cheap gates fast and shard long suites (for example, `--shard i/n`) based on measured wall-clock times. Set `timeout-minutes` explicitly. Add a workflow test that enforces a ceiling of 30 minutes and a named, numerically capped list of documented exceptions. For a reusable workflow, check the jobs inside the called workflow.

Within a job, schedule independent tasks in descending measured duration with a bounded worker pool. Start the longest tasks first and fill free slots with short tasks. Set the worker count to fit the runner's CPU, memory, and service limits. Keep dependent tasks in order and propagate task failures.

### 6. Changeset-Based Versioning

All templates use a changeset system that:

- **Eliminates merge conflicts** - Each PR creates an independent changeset file
### 14. Lint the Workflows Themselves

**The pipeline is code, and nothing lints it by default.** Workflow files accumulate shell quoting bugs, over-broad `permissions`, unpinned actions and template-injection sinks that no job in the pipeline is looking for, because every job is busy checking the application.

Two complementary tools, in their own workflow, triggered on changes to `.github/`:

- [`actionlint`](https://github.com/rhysd/actionlint) — syntax, expressions, and (crucially) the shell inside every `run:` block.
- [`zizmor`](https://docs.zizmor.sh/) — security audits: `excessive-permissions`, `unpinned-uses`, `template-injection`, `artipacked`.

```yaml
- uses: docker://rhysd/actionlint:1.7.12
  with:
    args: -color
```

- **Run actionlint as the Docker image, not a bare binary.** The image bundles `shellcheck` and `pyflakes`. A binary without `shellcheck` on `PATH` silently skips every shell check and exits 0 — so a green local run means nothing. This one detail is the difference between finding fourteen shell bugs and finding none.
- **Prefer annotations to SARIF** for zizmor unless code scanning is enabled everywhere the workflow runs. SARIF upload fails silently on forks; annotations fail loudly in both.
- **Set a confidence floor, not a severity floor.** `--min-confidence medium` filters by how sure the tool is, not by how bad the finding is. Review what falls below the floor once and record the decision, rather than discovering later that the floor was hiding a real finding.
- **Scope suppressions to a file, and write down when they can be removed.** A blanket `ignore` is indistinguishable from no gate at all.

### 15. Audit the Dependency Tree

**Code scanning does not audit your dependencies, and PR-scoped dependency review does not audit the ones you already have.** These two jobs look like coverage together and leave a hole between them: CodeQL analyses your source, while `dependency-review-action` runs only on `pull_request` and only inspects the dependencies a PR _changes_. An advisory published against a package that has been pinned for a year is invisible to both, forever, because no PR touches that line.

```yaml
- run: npm audit --package-lock-only --audit-level=high
```

- **Audit the lockfile as committed** (`--package-lock-only`). It reports what a consumer would get, and cannot be turned green by a resolution that only happens on this runner.
- **Put the job on the schedule**, not only on push. A scheduled run is the only thing that can notice an advisory published after the code stopped changing.
- **Set the level explicitly.** The default is `low`, which trains everyone to ignore the job; no flag at all is a different failure from a deliberate `--audit-level=high`.

### 16. Prove You Can Publish Before You Build

**A pull request exists to test the code; a push to the default branch exists to produce a release.** Those are different jobs, and a missing credential means different things to each. On a pull request it is a warning — forks have no secrets, and the code can still be tested. On the default branch it is the answer: if any credential needed for any planned release is unusable, nothing the run does afterwards can produce a release, and every minute spent building is waste.

Put a `preflight` job first and make every publishing job `needs:` it.

```yaml
release-preflight:
  runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
  permissions:
    contents: read
    id-token: wri… it
  steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v7
    - env:
        PREFLIGHT_MODE: ${{ github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && 'release' || 'report' }}
      run: node scripts/preflight-credentials.mjs --mode "$PREFLIGHT_MODE"

release:
  needs: [release-preflight]
  if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.release-preflight.result == 'success' }}
```

- **Probe with a write, not with a login.** ghcr.io's token endpoint returns 200 for any scope and verifies nothing — the push then fails 403. docker.io answers an anonymous push-scope request with 200 and a pull-only `access` claim. Open a blob upload session (`POST /v2/<repo>/blobs/uploads/`) and cancel it with `DELETE <Location>`: one round trip, nothing stored, and the only form of the check that is not a guess.
- **Report every failure, not the first.** The preflight's value is one report naming all missing credentials. A login step that aborts the job hides the rest, so make it `continue-on-error: true` and let the preflight script decide.
- **Check reachability, not just writability.** A GHCR package is private on first push and stays private until someone clicks; publishing more versions of a package nobody can pull is exactly the compute this job exists to skip. GitHub exposes no API for package visibility (the packages REST API is GET/DELETE/restore only), so this is a manual step that the pipeline can only detect and name.
- **Prefer trusted publishing.** A credential that expires is a release outage waiting for a calendar date. npm (`id-token: [REDACTED].
- **Verify the published result anonymously, and separately.** Never gate the release on the push (a failed mirror must not delete a good release), but do check afterwards, with no credentials, that what you published can be pulled. A check that authenticates measures the publisher's view; a reader gets neither the login nor the benefit of the doubt.
- **Report `unknown`, never a guess.** A registry that times out or answers HTTP 429 has not said the credential is broken, and a run in which nothing could be verified is not a pass. Say which of the two happened: "0 verified, 3 unknown" is actionable, "no failures" is not.
- **Measure the tarball before you upload it.** npm refused `@link-assistant/hive-mind` 2.40.0 and 2.40.1 with `E413 Payload Too Large` after every build had passed (2.40.1's tarball was 249,862,346 bytes); the largest tarball it is known to have accepted here is 165,142,849 bytes. Gate the actual archive below that (`npm pack --dry-run --json | node scripts/check-npm-tarball-size.mjs --stdin`) and name its largest files. An E413 is deterministic, so fail on the first one instead of retrying. Ship platform-specific binaries as per-platform packages pinned by `optionalDependencies`, as `@openai/codex` does (#4050, `src/native-codex/PACKAGES.md`).

### 17. Tell a Broken Pipeline from a Changed World

**A job that fails for a reason no commit can fix is a false negative, and it trains everyone to ignore red.** Issue #2625 found four of them on `main` at once: a dependency gate that failed every push because a new upstream major had appeared, a cleanup that failed every day because a ruleset forbids deleting branches, a dispatch that GitHub refused before it started, and a log upload that retried a refusal three times. Each one hid the real failures next to it.

```yaml
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      bump_type:
        required: true
        default: patch # the dispatch API answers HTTP 422 without it
```

- **Gate external state on pull requests; on push, warn.** "A newer version was published" is a fact about the world, not about the commit. Failing the push skips lint, tests and the release for a change that broke nothing; the pull request is where someone can act on it.
- **A policy refusal is a decision, not a transient error.** `Resource not accessible by integration` (a workflow `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot create gists) and a ruleset's `Repository rule violations found` answer the same way on every attempt. Retry `HTTP 429` and `5xx`; report a refusal once, name what would allow it, and move on.
- **Every input a workflow is dispatched with by API needs a default.** `gh workflow run` cannot fill a form: a `required: true` input without `default:` makes GitHub answer `HTTP 422: Required input '<name>' not provided`, and the run never exists. Test that each dispatched workflow accepts exactly the inputs its caller passes.
- **Create what you depend on, or tolerate its absence.** `gh pr edit --add-label` fails with `'<label>' not found` in a repository that never had the label. Create it on first use (`gh label create`) instead of failing a run that already did its work.
- **Write logs where the upload step looks.** An artifact step that finds nothing warns `No files were found with the provided path` and passes; the run that failed early, the one the artifact exists for, leaves no evidence. Make a missing log fail loudly in the test suite, not silently in production.
- **Say why a job skipped.** A downstream workflow that skips because its upstream failed is correct, but a green run that silently did nothing reads as "tested". Print the reason as a `::notice::` annotation so it shows on the run summary (issue #2923).
- **One outcome, one message.** A log that says "recovered and completed successfully" and then "❌ Agent reported error" for the same error sends readers down the wrong path. Compute the verdict first, then log only what is true.
- **A green bot run can still be stuck.** Dependabot logs `Deferring creation of a new pull request` and exits green while an open group pull request exists, even after a newer major superseded it (dependabot/dependabot-core#16791). Pull request #2285 stayed open 52 days and collected 37 "Dependabot is rebasing this PR" banners while every daily run passed. Check the outcome, not the exit status: the Dependabot Health workflow fails when a bot pull request is older than 14 days or carries more than 2 rebase banners (issue #4055).
- **Configure only what exists.** A Dependabot `docker-compose` entry for compose files that build every image locally matches no dependency and warns `groups where no dependencies match` on every run. Derive the ecosystem list from the repository and test it (issue #4055).
- **Group repeated failures by meaning, not by text.** A health check that keys failures by their exact message counts `Could not pull …:2.40.0` and `…:2.40.1` as two faults, so twelve identical failures never reach a threshold of five. Strip versions, ids, hashes and paths before comparing (issue #4055).
- **Wait for asynchronous release with a bound.** An async database pool closes its connections on a worker thread after `close()` returns. A step that needs "no open handles" right afterwards must poll with backoff and a deadline and name the holder it waited for, instead of failing on the first look (issue #4055).
- **A reply GitHub cut off is a transient fault, but only a read may repeat it.** When GitHub answers an HTTP error with an empty or truncated body, `gh` prints only `unexpected end of JSON input`, without the status code. Retry that message for reads (`GET`, `gh pr view`, GraphQL queries), never for writes: a write may already have happened (issue #2571). A polling loop must also survive a few failed polls in a row instead of failing the job on the first one (issue #4149).
- **Take a dispatched run from the dispatch response, not from a listing.** `gh run list --workflow --branch` can stay empty for minutes after the run was created. `POST …/actions/workflows/{workflow}/dispatches` with `return_run_details: true` returns `workflow_run_id` and `html_url`. If the run still cannot be found, warn: the dispatch succeeded, and the job that collects the results reports a run that never started (issue #4149).

### 5. Fast-Fail Job Ordering

**Run fast checks before slow checks** to give the fastest possible feedback:

```
Fast checks (~7-30s each):     Slow checks (~1-10 min each):
├── test-compilation            ├── test-suites (unit tests)
├── lint (format + ESLint)      ├── test-execution (integration)
└── check-file-line-limits      ├── docker-pr-check
                                └── helm-pr-check
```

Gate slow checks on fast checks:

```yaml
test-suites:
  needs: [test-compilation, lint, check-file-line-limits]
  if: |
    always() &&
    !cancelled() &&
    !contains(needs.*.result, 'failure') &&
    needs.test-compilation.result == 'success' &&
    needs.lint.result == 'success' &&
    needs.check-file-line-limits.result == 'success'
```

#### Size jobs and start the longest work first

Aim for roughly 5–30 minutes per substantial runner job. Keep cheap gates fast and shard long suites (for example, `--shard i/n`) based on measured wall-clock times. Set `timeout-minutes` explicitly. Add a workflow test that enforces a ceiling of 30 minutes and a named, numerically capped list of documented exceptions. For a reusable workflow, check the jobs inside the called workflow.

Within a job, schedule independent tasks in descending measured duration with a bounded worker pool. Start the longest tasks first and fill free slots with short tasks. Set the worker count to fit the runner's CPU, memory, and service limits. Keep dependent tasks in order and propagate task failures.

### 6. Changeset-Based Versioning

All templates use a changeset system that:

- **Eliminates merge conflicts** - Each PR creates an independent changeset file
### 14. Lint the Workflows Themselves

**The pipeline is code, and nothing lints it by default.** Workflow files accumulate shell quoting bugs, over-broad `permissions`, unpinned actions and template-injection sinks that no job in the pipeline is looking for, because every job is busy checking the application.

Two complementary tools, in their own workflow, triggered on changes to `.github/`:

- [`actionlint`](https://github.com/rhysd/actionlint) — syntax, expressions, and (crucially) the shell inside every `run:` block.
- [`zizmor`](https://docs.zizmor.sh/) — security audits: `excessive-permissions`, `unpinned-uses`, `template-injection`, `artipacked`.

```yaml
- uses: docker://rhysd/actionlint:1.7.12
  with:
    args: -color
```

- **Run actionlint as the Docker image, not a bare binary.** The image bundles `shellcheck` and `pyflakes`. A binary without `shellcheck` on `PATH` silently skips every shell check and exits 0 — so a green local run means nothing. This one detail is the difference between finding fourteen shell bugs and finding none.
- **Prefer annotations to SARIF** for zizmor unless code scanning is enabled everywhere the workflow runs. SARIF upload fails silently on forks; annotations fail loudly in both.
- **Set a confidence floor, not a severity floor.** `--min-confidence medium` filters by how sure the tool is, not by how bad the finding is. Review what falls below the floor once and record the decision, rather than discovering later that the floor was hiding a real finding.
- **Scope suppressions to a file, and write down when they can be removed.** A blanket `ignore` is indistinguishable from no gate at all.

### 15. Audit the Dependency Tree

**Code scanning does not audit your dependencies, and PR-scoped dependency review does not audit the ones you already have.** These two jobs look like coverage together and leave a hole between them: CodeQL analyses your source, while `dependency-review-action` runs only on `pull_request` and only inspects the dependencies a PR _changes_. An advisory published against a package that has been pinned for a year is invisible to both, forever, because no PR touches that line.

```yaml

```
