"""Inventory CI inputs from link-cli and downloaded recursive template trees."""

import json
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
TEMPLATES = ("rust", "js", "csharp", "python", "java", "cpp")


def ci_input(path: str) -> bool:
    """Include workflow-owned files, CI helpers, hooks, and root CI policies."""
    filename = Path(path).name
    return (
        path.startswith(
            (
                ".github/",
                ".githooks/",
                ".husky/",
                ".ci/",
                ".config/",
                "ci/",
                "scripts/",
                "parity/",
            )
        )
        or re.match(r"^(csharp|js|rust)/scripts/", path) is not None
        or re.search(
            r"^\.(pre-commit|lychee|secretlint|actionlint|zizmor|codecov|package-registry-manager"
            r"|prettier|editorconfig|clang-format|shellcheck)",
            filename,
        )
        is not None
        or filename.startswith(("eslint.config.", "rustfmt."))
    )


def stem(path: str) -> str:
    return Path(path).stem.replace("_", "-")


def purpose(path: str) -> str:
    matched = (
        (
            "change detection and stage gate",
            r"detect|fresh-merge|javascript-first|javascript-stage|parity",
        ),
        (
            "registry and release",
            r"version|changelog|changeset|release|publish|registry|npm|pypi|nuget|crates|vcpkg|maven|package",
        ),
        (
            "workflow validation and status",
            r"workflow|status|gate|policy|concurrency|zizmor|actionlint",
        ),
        (
            "security and dependencies",
            r"security|secrets|codeql|audit|depend|sarif|credential|preflight",
        ),
        ("documentation and links", r"docs|lychee|links|web-archive|pages"),
        (
            "runner and artifact handling",
            r"runner|unacquired|rerun|artifact|archive|budget|buildx",
        ),
        (
            "source and test quality",
            r"lint|format|file-size|line-limit|coverage|warnings|test",
        ),
    )
    for description, pattern in matched:
        if re.search(pattern, path):
            return description
    return "repository or language-specific infrastructure"


def main() -> None:
    directory = Path(sys.argv[1])
    base = sys.argv[2]
    local_tree = subprocess.check_output(
        ["git", "ls-tree", "-rz", base], cwd=ROOT, text=True
    )
    local = {}
    for entry in local_tree.rstrip("\0").split("\0"):
        metadata, path = entry.split("\t", 1)
        if ci_input(path):
            local[path] = metadata.split()[2]
    snapshots = {"link-cli": local}
    template_paths = {}
    for name in TEMPLATES:
        tree = json.loads((directory / f"{name}-tree.json").read_text())["tree"]
        snapshot = {
            file["path"]: file["sha"]
            for file in tree
            if file["type"] == "blob" and ci_input(file["path"])
        }
        template_paths.update(
            {f"{name}/{path}": digest for path, digest in snapshot.items()}
        )
        snapshots[name] = snapshot

    print("repository\tpath\tblob\tpurpose\tother repository matches")
    for name, snapshot in snapshots.items():
        other = template_paths if name == "link-cli" else local
        for path, blob in sorted(snapshot.items()):
            peers = [
                f"{item} ({'identical' if digest == blob else 'same stem'})"
                for item, digest in other.items()
                if digest == blob or stem(item) == stem(path)
            ]
            print(name, path, blob, purpose(path), ", ".join(peers) or "-", sep="\t")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
"}

#### Size jobs and start the longest work first

# actionlint cannot see workflow security defects: unpinned third-party
      # actions, checkouts that persist GITHUB_TOKEN in .git/config, or
      # template injection into `run:` blocks. zizmor covers those.
      #
      # Only .github is audited: dev/log keeps verbatim copies of the template
      # workflows as evidence, and they are not run here.
      #
      # The action's wheel lock can lag behind PyPI releases. Verify the
      # wheel against our own lock and share the install between both audits.
      - name: Install the locked zizmor wheel
        run: |
          python3 -m pip install --require-hashes --only-binary=:all: --no-deps \
            --target "$RUNNER_TEMP/zizmor" -r .github/scripts/requirements-workflow-audit.txt

      # Emit annotations so findings fail the job without code scanning.
      - name: Audit workflow files
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/zizmor/bin/zizmor" --format github --config .github/zizmor.yml .github

      # The audits that cover container image references (`unpinned-images`
      # among them) are pedantic-only, so the hash-pin policy is not enforced
      # against `uses: docker://` by the regular pass above. Narrowing this
      # pass to high severity and high confidence keeps that enforcement
      # without the stylistic noise of the pedantic persona.
      - name: Audit for pedantic-only high-severity findings
        timeout-minutes: 5
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/zizmor/bin/zizmor" --config .github/zizmor.yml \
            --persona pedantic --min-severity high --min-confidence high \
            .github

    = note: audit confidence → High
    = help: audit documentation → https://docs.zizmor.sh/audits/#undocumented-permissions

name: JavaScript stage

# The JavaScript stage of the stage gate (issue #111): ESLint and Prettier,
# every Node unit test (`npm run test:js`) and the cross-language parity
# checker. It needs no Rust, wasm-pack or .NET, so it finishes in a few
# minutes.
#
# Every workflow that runs Rust or C# calls this file as its first job
# (`javascript: uses: ./.github/workflows/javascript-stage.yml`) and lists
# `javascript` in the `needs:` of each Rust or C# job, so those jobs start
# only after this stage succeeded for the same commit. A failed, cancelled or
# skipped stage leaves them skipped. .github/scripts/workflow-policy.test.mjs
# enforces that wiring. javascript.yml runs the same stage on its own for
# every pull request, with no path filter, behind the required
# "Pipeline Status (javascript)" check.

on:
  workflow_call:

permissions:
  contents: read

# Provide Git config to actions/checkout itself; checkout runs git init before
# any workflow step can configure Git, which otherwise prints the
# default-branch hint into every log.
env:
  GIT_CONFIG_COUNT: '1'
  GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0: ini…nch
  GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0: main

jobs:
  stage:
    name: JavaScript stage
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 15
    # In a called workflow, github.workflow is the caller's name, so each
    # caller cancels only its own superseded stage.
    concurrency:
      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.action == 'synchronize' && github.ref || github.event_name == 'push' && github.sha || github.run_id }}-javascript-stage
      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.action == 'synchronize' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          # The parity checker compares the manifest with the base commit.

      matrix:

    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    timeout-minutes: 45
    concurrency:
      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.action == 'synchronize' && github.ref || github.event_name == 'push' && github.sha || github.run_id }}-interop-${{ matrix.os }}
      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.action == 'synchronize' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '26.x'
      - name: Setup Rust
        shell: bash
        run: rustup toolchain install stable --profile minimal --no-self-update
      - name: Build Rust CLI
        run: cargo build --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --locked --bin clink -j 2
      - uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v6
        with:
          dotnet-version: '10.0.403'
      - name: Build C# CLI
        run: dotnet build csharp/Foundation.Data.Doublets.Cli/Foundation.Data.Doublets.Cli.csproj -c Release
      - name: Every kind between the Rust and C# servers and relays and the Rust, C# and JS clients
        shell: bash
        run: |
          export CLINK_BIN="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/rust/target/debug/clink"
          node examples/ipc/interop.mjs --js \
            rust=rust/target/debug/clink \
            'csharp=["dotnet","csharp/Foundation.Data.Doublets.Cli/bin/Release/net10.0/clink.dll"]'
      - name: The JS client against the Rust server over every kind
        shell: bash
        working-directory: js/client
        run: |
          export CLINK_BIN="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/rust/target/debug/clink"
          node --test --test-concurrency=1 --test-timeout=120000 test/ipc.test.mjs

  pipeline-status:
    name: Pipeline Status (ipc)
    needs:
      - javascript

    if: ${{ !cancelled() }}

tools.description:
Waits on a yielded `exec` cell and returns new output or completion.
- Use `wait` only after `exec` returns `Script running with cell ID ...`.
- `cell_id` identifies the running `exec` cell to resume.
- `yield_time_ms` controls how long to wait for more output before yielding again. Defaults to 10000 ms.
- `max_tokens` limits how much new output this wait call returns. Defaults to 10000 tokens.
- `terminate: true` stops the running cell; false or omitted waits for output.
- `wait` returns only the new output since the last yield, or the final completion or termination result for that cell.
- If the cell is still running, `wait` may yield again with the same `cell_id`.
- If the cell has already finished, `wait` returns the completed result and closes the cell.

content.text:
You are Codex, an agent based on GPT-6. You and the user share a workspace, and your job is to collaborate with them until their intended goal is completely achieved.

# Completing the user's task

Persist until you've completed the task the user asked for. Avoid stopping to end the turn while the task is incomplete or if there is an authorized next step you can take, and instead take the next steps within task scope to progress the user's request. Make sure that you have accounted for every part of the user's request, and persist until you've delivered a result that fully satisfies the user's goal. Clarify with the user only if there is significant task scope change or for irreversible destructive actions.

If your final response before ending the turn is a suggested next step, a plan, a request to the user for a routine decision, instructions for a task to execute, or similar handoff to the user, take these steps yourself to make progress towards what the user asked for (only if you have authorization to do so, and while flagging any assumptions to the user). Only stop if you are concretely blocked, have a decision that the user needs to resolve, policy requires you to clarify with the user, or you require authorization to proceed.

# Personality

As Codex, you are a curious, thoughtful collaborator and a clear communicator. You keep your own judgment, disagree constructively when you have reason, and reconsider when the evidence warrants it. You let your interest and personality emerge naturally, without flattery or forced enthusiasm.

## Writing style

Write as a user’s colleague would: clear, professional, and using terminology the user and sources use. Keep technical details and use domain-specific language when they make the explanation more precise. Use the active voice and keep closely related details together. Cover the key points up front, and avoid references that the reader can only make sense of later in the response. Give the user enough context to follow your reasoning. 

Do not invent jargon, new terms, or metaphors. Use established names or a short explanation instead. Do not invent shorthand naming, internal implementation labels, and unnecessary process narration.

Do not repeat a previous point or insight with a declarative sentence. Do not declare what you're about to explain or praise the strength of your available evidence. agents_md.text:
# Rules for AI agents working on link-cli

Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) first; everything in it applies to
agents. This file adds the rules that agents in particular have broken
before.

## The single-pusher rule for CI/CD fixes

1. **Exactly one agent pushes to a branch.** Sub-agents and parallel workers
   never push. They return their patch or commit to the coordinating agent,
   which is the only one that pushes.
2. **Never push while a run is in progress on the same branch.** Before every
   push, run this and wait until it prints `0`:

   ```bash
   gh run list --branch "$(git branch --show-current)" --json status \
     --jq '[.[] | select(.status != "completed")] | length'
   ```

3. **Push only after every failure of the last run is fixed.** For each
   failed job:
   - save the log (`gh run view <run-id> --log-failed > ci-logs/<name>-<run-id>.log`)
   - find the root cause
   - fix it, and verify the fix locally

   Then push once. Do not push to "see if CI passes", and do not push one fix
   per failure.
4. Do not push only to retry an infrastructure failure, such as a runner that
   was never acquired. `rerun-infrastructure-failures.yml` reruns those.

## Pull requests are never closed for age

There is no stale pull request policy, and there must never be one. Do not
close, label as stale or rebase an open pull request because it is old or
idle, and do not add a workflow (such as `actions/stale`) that would. An old
pull request is work that can still continue. Close one only when its owner
asks for it.

## Stage order and parity

- The JavaScript stage runs first: lint, `npm run test:js` and
  `node parity/check-parity.mjs`. When it fails, no Rust or C# job runs, so
  fix it first.
- Any new workflow job that installs or runs Rust (`cargo`, `rustup`,
  `wasm-pack`) or .NET (`dotnet`, `actions/setup-dotnet`) must:
  - list `javascript` in its `needs:`, where the `javascript` job calls
    `./.github/workflows/javascript-stage.yml`;
  - and, if its `if:` uses `always()` or `!cancelled()`, also require
    `needs.javascript.result == 'success'`.

  `workflow-policy.test.mjs` enforces this.
- When you change a feature in one implementation, either:
  - change the others in the same pull request, or
  - record a reasoned `--acknowledge` in `parity/features.json`.

  Never edit fingerprints by hand; run `node parity/check-parity.mjs --update`.
  See [docs/PARITY.md](docs/PARITY.md).
- Do not weaken a check to make CI pass. That covers path filters on
  `rust.yml`, `csharp.yml` and `javascript.yml`, skipping the golden fixture
  test, and disabling a policy test. Fix the cause instead.

## Working conventions

- Keep experiments in `experiments/` and runnable examples in `examples/`.
- Every source file stays at or below 1000 lines. The linters warn from 900.
- Add a `rust/changelog.d/` fragment or a `csharp/.changeset/` file for each
  package you change.
- Case studies of non-trivial issues go in `docs/case-studies/issue-<n>/`.

# Cross-language parity

link-cli has three implementations: C# in `csharp/`, Rust in `rust/`, and
JavaScript in `js/`. Before issue #111, nothing in CI noticed when a feature
changed in one of them and not in the others. Two files now make parity
checkable, and the JavaScript stage checks them before any Rust or C# job
starts (see [CI stages](ci-cd/troubleshooting.md#stages)).

| File                          | What it records                                                                                |
| ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `parity/features.json`        | Every CLI and library feature, with its status, sources and tests in C#, Rust and JavaScript.  |
| `parity/golden-fixtures.json` | The shared `docs/protocol` fixtures that the C#, Rust and JavaScript test suites must load.    |
| `parity/check-parity.mjs`     | The checker. It has no dependencies, and its header lists every command.                       |

## The feature manifest

Each entry in `features[]` has an `id`, a `title`, and one cell per language.

| `status`         | Meaning                                                   | Required fields                                                   |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `implemented`    | The language has its own implementation.                  | `sources` and `tests` (globs), plus the `fingerprint` the checker writes |
| `delegated`      | Another language's code does the work.                    | `to` (the language that implements it), and `via` (the binding globs) |
| `not-applicable` | The feature has no meaning in this language.              | `reason`                                                          |
| `missing`        | The feature should exist here but does not yet.           | `issue` (a tracking issue URL)                                    |

An implemented cell can also record platform or runtime limits in `scope`.
Those cells participate in fingerprint and parity checks.

Each language also lists `roots`: globs of its source files. A source file
under a root must belong to a feature, or to a `shared` entry with a reason.
This rule is what makes a new file count against the manifest instead of
slipping past it.

## What the checker rejects

`node parity/check-parity.mjs` fails, and lists every finding, when any of
these holds:

1. The manifest breaks the schema: an unknown status, or a missing `tests`,
   `issue`, `to` or `reason`.
2. A glob matches no tracked file, for example because a file was renamed.
3. A source file under a language root belongs to no feature.
4. A recorded fingerprint is stale: the code changed and the manifest did not.
5. **One-sided change.** Compared with the base commit, only some of a
   feature's `implemented` cells changed, and no `parityExceptions` entry
   acknowledges exactly those new fingerprints.
6. `parity/golden-fixtures.json` disagrees with the fixture files. This covers
   a hash mismatch, a fixture missing from the manifest, a fixture with no C#,
   Rust or JavaScript consumer test, and a consumer test that no longer
   mentions its fixture.
7. A golden fixture is not marked `-text` in `.gitattributes`. Without it,
   git on Windows (`core.autocrlf=true`) checks the fixture out with CRLF
   line endings, and its hash no longer matches.
8. With `--receipt`: a test suite did not report loading every golden fixture
   with the expected hash.

The JavaScript stage passes the base commit as `PARITY_BASE_SHA`. On a pull
request that is the pull request's base; on a push it is the commit before
the push. The stage checks out with `fetch-depth: 0`. If that commit is
missing from the clone, the checker fails. It never skips rule 5 silently.

## Daily use

```bash
# Check the working tree against main, as CI does on a pull request.
node parity/check-parity.mjs --base origin/main

# Print every matched file and fingerprint.
node parity/check-parity.mjs --base origin/main --verbose   # or PARITY_DEBUG=1

# After changing code, refresh the fingerprints and fixture hashes.
node parity/check-parity.mjs --update

# A change that is deliberately one-sided, such as a Rust-only performance fix.
node parity/check-parity.mjs --base origin/main --acknowledge <feature-id> \
  --reason "Rust-only performance fix; behaviour is unchanged" \
  --ref https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/pull/<n>
```

An acknowledgement covers only the fingerprints it records. If the same
feature changes again on one side, the checker needs a new acknowledgement.

When you add a feature:

1. Add its entry to `parity/features.json`, with an honest status for each
   language.
2. Run `--update`.

A `missing` cell links the issue that tracks the gap.

## Golden fixtures

Golden fixtures are the files under `docs/protocol/` that match
`include` in `parity/golden-fixtures.json`. All three suites have to load them:

- Rust: `rust/tests/golden_fixtures_tests.rs`
- C#: `csharp/Foundation.Data.Doublets.Cli.Tests/GoldenFixturesTests.cs`
- JavaScript: `js/test/golden-fixtures.test.mjs`, run by `npm run test:js`

Each test reads every listed fixture and checks its SHA-256. When the
`GOLDEN_FIXTURES_RECEIPT` variable is set, the test also writes a receipt,
`{ "suite", "fixtures": { path: sha256 } }`. In `rust.yml`, `csharp.yml` and
`javascript-stage.yml`, the step after the tests runs
`node parity/check-parity.mjs --receipt <suite> <file>`. If a suite filtered
the test out, skipped it, or was not built, the receipt is missing or
incomplete and CI fails.

To change a fixture:

1. Edit the file.
2. Run `node parity/check-parity.mjs --update`.
3. Make all three suites pass.

To add a fixture, list it with at least one C#, one Rust and one JavaScript
consumer test that mentions its file name. The JavaScript consumers are the
tests in `js/client/test` and `js/server/test` that read the fixture.

## Related

- [JS-WORKBENCH.md](JS-WORKBENCH.md) lists what `js/` implements itself and
  what it delegates to the Rust WebAssembly build.
- [ci-cd/troubleshooting.md](ci-cd/troubleshooting.md) explains how to read a
  failed parity check in CI.
- [case-studies/issue-111](case-studies/issue-111/README.md) records why the
  gate exists.

link-cli has three implementations: C# in `csharp/`, Rust in `rust/`, and
JavaScript in `js/`. Before issue #111, nothing in CI noticed when a feature
changed in one of them and not in the others. Two files now make parity
checkable, and the JavaScript stage checks them before any Rust or C# job
starts (see [CI stages](ci-cd/troubleshooting.md#stages)).

| File                          | What it records                                                                                |
| ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `parity/features.json`        | Every CLI and library feature, with its status, sources and tests in C#, Rust and JavaScript.  |
| `parity/golden-fixtures.json` | The shared `docs/protocol` fixtures that the C#, Rust and JavaScript test suites must load.    |
| `parity/check-parity.mjs`     | The checker. It has no dependencies, and its header lists every command.                       |

## The feature manifest

Each entry in `features[]` has an `id`, a `title`, and one cell per language.

| `status`         | Meaning                                                   | Required fields                                                   |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `implemented`    | The language has its own implementation.                  | `sources` and `tests` (globs), plus the `fingerprint` the checker writes |
| `delegated`      | Another language's code does the work.                    | `to` (the language that implements it), and `via` (the binding globs) |
| `not-applicable` | The feature has no meaning in this language.              | `reason`                                                          |
| `missing`        | The feature should exist here but does not yet.           | `issue` (a tracking issue URL)                                    |

An implemented cell can also record platform or runtime limits in `scope`.
Those cells participate in fingerprint and parity checks.

Each language also lists `roots`: globs of its source files. A source file
under a root must belong to a feature, or to a `shared` entry with a reason.
This rule is what makes a new file count against the manifest instead of
slipping past it.

## What the checker rejects

`node parity/check-parity.mjs` fails, and lists every finding, when any of
these holds:

1. The manifest breaks the schema: an unknown status, or a missing `tests`,
   `issue`, `to` or `reason`.
2. A glob matches no tracked file, for example because a file was renamed.
3. A source file under a language root belongs to no feature.
4. A recorded fingerprint is stale: the code changed and the manifest did not.
5. **One-sided change.** Compared with the base commit, only some of a
   feature's `implemented` cells changed, and no `parityExceptions` entry
   acknowledges exactly those new fingerprints.
6. `parity/golden-fixtures.json` disagrees with the fixture files. This covers
   a hash mismatch, a fixture missing from the manifest, a fixture with no C#,
   Rust or JavaScript consumer test, and a consumer test that no longer
   mentions its fixture.
7. A golden fixture is not marked `-text` in `.gitattributes`. Without it,
   git on Windows (`core.autocrlf=true`) checks the fixture out with CRLF
   line endings, and its hash no longer matches.
8. With `--receipt`: a test suite did not report loading every golden fixture
   with the expected hash.

The JavaScript stage passes the base commit as `PARITY_BASE_SHA`. On a pull
request that is the pull request's base; on a push it is the commit before
the push. The stage checks out with `fetch-depth: 0`. If that commit is
missing from the clone, the checker fails. It never skips rule 5 silently.

## Daily use

```bash
# Check the working tree against main, as CI does on a pull request.
node parity/check-parity.mjs --base origin/main

# Print every matched file and fingerprint.
node parity/check-parity.mjs --base origin/main --verbose   # or PARITY_DEBUG=1

# After changing code, refresh the fingerprints and fixture hashes.
node parity/check-parity.mjs --update

# A change that is deliberately one-sided, such as a Rust-only performance fix.
node parity/check-parity.mjs --base origin/main --acknowledge <feature-id> \
  --reason "Rust-only performance fix; behaviour is unchanged" \
  --ref https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/pull/<n>
```

An acknowledgement covers only the fingerprints it records. If the same
feature changes again on one side, the checker needs a new acknowledgement.

When you add a feature:

1. Add its entry to `parity/features.json`, with an honest status for each
   language.
2. Run `--update`.

A `missing` cell links the issue that tracks the gap.

## Golden fixtures

Golden fixtures are the files under `docs/protocol/` that match
`include` in `parity/golden-fixtures.json`. All three suites have to load them:

- Rust: `rust/tests/golden_fixtures_tests.rs`
- C#: `csharp/Foundation.Data.Doublets.Cli.Tests/GoldenFixturesTests.cs`
- JavaScript: `js/test/golden-fixtures.test.mjs`, run by `npm run test:js`

Each test reads every listed fixture and checks its SHA-256. When the
`GOLDEN_FIXTURES_RECEIPT` variable is set, the test also writes a receipt,
`{ "suite", "fixtures": { path: sha256 } }`. In `rust.yml`, `csharp.yml` and
`javascript-stage.yml`, the step after the tests runs
`node parity/check-parity.mjs --receipt <suite> <file>`. If a suite filtered
the test out, skipped it, or was not built, the receipt is missing or
incomplete and CI fails.

To change a fixture:

1. Edit the file.
2. Run `node parity/check-parity.mjs --update`.
3. Make all three suites pass.

To add a fixture, list it with at least one C#, one Rust and one JavaScript
consumer test that mentions its file name. The JavaScript consumers are the
tests in `js/client/test` and `js/server/test` that read the fixture.

- [JS-WORKBENCH.md](JS-WORKBENCH.md) lists what `js/` implements itself and

- [ci-cd/troubleshooting.md](ci-cd/troubleshooting.md) explains how to read a
  failed parity check in CI.
- [case-studies/issue-111](case-studies/issue-111/README.md) records why the
  gate exists.

# Local mirror of the cheap CI gates, so the same defects fail on `git commit`
# instead of ten minutes into a workflow run. Ported from the AI driven
# development pipeline templates for issue #96 and adapted to this monorepo:
# every hook has to point at the stack-specific manifest, because the three
# projects live under csharp/, rust/ and js/.
#
# Install once with:
#   pip install pre-commit && pre-commit install
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/pre-commit/pre-commit-hooks
    rev: v5.0.0
    # Preserve verbatim investigation inputs, including large compressed logs.
    # The separate secrets hook still checks all tracked evidence.
    exclude: ^(dev/log/|docs/case-studies/)
    hooks:
      - id: trailing-whitespace
      - id: end-of-file-fixer
      - id: check-yaml
      - id: check-json
      - id: check-toml
      - id: check-xml
      - id: check-merge-conflict
      - id: check-added-large-files

  - repo: local
    hooks:
      # Mirrors the "Lint and Format Check" job of rust.yml.
      - id: cargo-fmt
        name: cargo fmt
        entry: cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all --
        language: system
        types: [rust]
        pass_filenames: false

      - id: cargo-clippy
        name: cargo clippy
        entry: cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
        language: system
        types: [rust]
        pass_filenames: false

      # Mirrors the "Lint and Format Check" job of csharp.yml. The solution sets
      # TreatWarningsAsErrors in csharp/Directory.Build.props, so a plain build
      # is already the warning gate.
      - id: dotnet-format
        name: dotnet format
        entry: dotnet format csharp --verify-no-changes
        language: system
        types: [c#]
        pass_filenames: false

      # Mirrors the workflow policy and repository layout guards. These are pure
      # Node with no dependencies, so they are fast enough for every commit.
      - id: workflow-policy
        name: workflow policy and repository layout tests
        entry: node --test .github/scripts/*.test.mjs js/test/*.test.mjs csharp/scripts/*.test.mjs
        language: system
        files: ^(\.github/|js/|csharp/|rust/|\.lycheeignore|README\.md)
        pass_filenames: false

      - id: javascript-quality
        name: JavaScript lint and formatting
        entry: node .github/scripts/check-javascript-quality.mjs
        language: system
        files: \.(js|mjs|cjs|jsx)$
        exclude: ^(dev/log/|docs/case-studies/)
        pass_filenames: false

      - id: secrets
        name: secrets in tracked files including ignored evidence
        entry: node .github/scripts/check-secrets.mjs
        language: system
        pass_filenames: false

      - id: python-quality
        name: Python lint, formatting and CI helper types
        entry: python .github/scripts/check-python-quality.py
        language: python
        additional_dependencies: [ruff==0.17.4, mypy==2.4.1]
        types: [python]
        exclude: ^(dev/log/|docs/case-studies/)
        pass_filenames: false

# Issue #207. CI reliability and template comparison

## Timeline

All times are UTC on 2026-11-27. The [evidence index](../../../dev/log/issues/207/pulls/208/README.md) links the original issue, draft and run records.

| Time | What happened |
| --- | --- |
| 19:54 | Workflows for merge `03f44dd` started. npm returned HTTP 404 for the server’s OIDC exchange at 19:54:57. |
| 19:57 | Issue #207 opened while the default-branch checks were still running. Its initial “0 not passing” counted conclusions that had yet to be posted. |
| 20:18–20:21 | After the C# release advanced `main` to `df8b0f8`, JS client conformance for `03f44dd` was cancelled while reopening native pages. The earlier Rust Windows test was cancelled mid-suite. Their status gates correctly rejected the cancellations. |
| 20:29–20:30 | The replacement JS client run failed its real etcd scenario. A paused node had been resumed before the test checked that the leader changed. |
| 20:57–21:00 | The issue update recorded the still-running Rust check. The generated initial commit of draft #208 added a root `.gitkeep`, and required JavaScript failed the layout guard. The failure propagated to dependent jobs. |
| After 21:00 | The Rust release advanced `main` to `d8a26c9`. The next server workflow again reported HTTP 404 for the same package. JS client conformance on the same main revision succeeded in both journal modes, confirming that the earlier leader assertion failed intermittently. The PR branch incorporated the new default-branch tip before the fixes. |
| 21:21 | PR #208 became ready for review and checks for `b2c74235` started. |
| 21:38–21:40 | The hosted conformance job passed the corrected real etcd scenario in both journal modes and uploaded the member logs. [Conformance job](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/actions/runs/46069793278/job/140744356887) |
| 21:53 | The Windows Rust suite and release jobs finished on `d8a26c9`. The JS server registry preflight remained the only failed workflow on that main revision. [Rust pipeline](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/actions/runs/46067149253) · [Server preflight](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/actions/runs/46067149214) |
| 22:11 | All 14 workflows passed on the first PR revision, `b2c74235`. Windows Rust passed the full suite, golden receipt check and native LSM example runs within its existing budget. [Rust pipeline](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/actions/runs/46069793342) |

## Requirements and verification

| Requirement | Cause, change and verification |
| --- | --- |
| Investigate every red or incomplete run named in the issue and follow its update | Job conclusions and compressed logs preserve the initial runs, the next two default-branch revisions, and the draft. Narrow diagnostics in the evidence index distinguish checkout policy, process elections, overlapping workflows, registry configuration, runner acquisition and upstream warnings. |
| Preserve required check coverage and dependency order | The draft placeholder broke `js/test/repositoryLayout.test.mjs`. Remove it, keep the layout test and keep all three required checks unfiltered. JavaScript lint, unit tests, receipts and parity still gate Rust and C#. |
| Keep each main commit and intentional run observable | Jobs formerly grouped by branch ref could cancel already-running checks and replace pending jobs. Read-only keys now use the push SHA or run ID, with a per-PR synchronize group. Each matrix keeps its identity. Shared release writers use GitHub’s `queue: max` with cancellation disabled. The workflow policy tests enforce the keys and writer configuration. |
| Fix the actual consensus assertion | Raft can choose a resumed member in a new election. Observe a majority-backed replacement while the original process is stopped, commit through the available quorum and then rejoin the former member. After recovery, require a healthy converged cluster and check the journal and stale-write guarantees. The focused regression rejects discordant and stale status samples. JS Client CI runs the real experiment in both journal modes. Manual dispatch accepts `verbose_consensus`, and `ETCD_TEST_VERBOSE=1` records member observations and etcd debug logs locally. |
| Test and release npm packages with appropriate credentials | PRs and ordinary manual runs validate the tarball without registry credentials. Both packages use the JS template's compressed size budget of 157 MiB. A failure names the largest files so it can be fixed before publishing. Main-only writers require successful preflight. A separate read-only job downloads the exact published version anonymously. Authentication-only dispatch continues to exercise the real OIDC exchange. Tests distinguish a package unavailable publicly, a public package with a missing or mismatched trust mapping, a registry outage and a successful exchange. |
| Run JS client and server CI for changes to their actual inputs | The client’s enumerated experiment paths missed the etcd harness. Cover the full experiment subtree, the shared stage and its policy inputs in both workflows, and the server’s embedded-store examples. Preserve the existing unit, portability and conformance jobs. |
| Resolve actionable CI warnings | Move Rust’s local transaction tests to a sibling module and centralize C# import option parsing in the existing I/O class. Both files are below the existing 900-line warning threshold. Parity fingerprints were updated with structural-change acknowledgements. Release fragments trigger the normal package release paths. |
| Compare all six template trees and apply applicable practices | The [file-level comparison](../../../dev/log/issues/207/pulls/208/templates/ci-file-comparison.tsv) enumerates workflows, supporting scripts, CI policy, hooks and matching files from pinned snapshots. The practice crosswalk below records equivalent local coverage and template differences. |
| Report shared defects where reproducible | The six template reports and the solver placeholder report include reproductions, temporary workarounds and code-level proposals. The existing Actionlint report tracks its rejected queue syntax. |
| Deliver one PR with evidence and release verification | [PR #208](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/pull/208) owns this work. Issue #207 had no required sub-issues or blocking-issue links when its timeline was captured. npm server release remains dependent on maintainer setup. |

## Template crosswalk

| Practice | Template implementations and link-cli decision |
| --- | --- |
| Preserve independent runs | All six templates had branch-scoped cancellation for one or more read-only checks on default-branch pushes. Rust, JS and Python had previously chosen that behavior. C# and C++ already separate writers. link-cli applies the newer guide’s event/revision policy across all sixteen workflow files and enables the existing upstream writer queue pattern. |
| Run cheap checks first and prove their provenance | Rust and JS contain JavaScript-first examples and policy helpers. link-cli requires a same-commit reusable stage and validates a golden-fixture receipt per language. Workflow policy caps job timeouts at 30 minutes, with named limits for native builds and registry waits. Python, Java and C++ examples assume standalone distributables and toolchains. Their language-specific release steps do not apply to the port and fixture code in this monorepo. |
| Validate scope and fixtures | The templates use change detection, fresh-merge checks, and size and docs gates. link-cli already uses whole-PR comparisons, fresh-merge simulation, conditional native jobs, strict required status, parity and explicit layout checks. The JS package path filters in this PR now include the shared stage, internal examples and all conformance inputs. |
| Keep full verification on the current PR revision | The guide offers a ready-for-review trigger paired with a separately required full-tier status. This repository requires JavaScript, Rust and C# pipeline statuses on every PR revision. It runs the applicable native jobs after the shared JavaScript stage and keeps the full check current on each synchronization. # Local mirror of the cheap CI gates, so the same defects fail on `git commit`
# instead of ten minutes into a workflow run. Ported from the AI driven
# development pipeline templates for issue #96 and adapted to this monorepo:
# every hook has to point at the stack-specific manifest, because the three
# projects live under csharp/, rust/ and js/.
#
# Install once with:
#   pip install pre-commit && pre-commit install
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/pre-commit/pre-commit-hooks
    rev: v5.0.0
    # Preserve verbatim investigation inputs, including large compressed logs.
    # The separate secrets hook still checks all tracked evidence.
    exclude: ^(dev/log/|docs/case-studies/)
    hooks:
      - id: trailing-whitespace
      - id: end-of-file-fixer
      - id: check-yaml
      - id: check-json
      - id: check-toml
      - id: check-xml
      - id: check-merge-conflict
      - id: check-added-large-files

  - repo: local
    hooks:
      # Mirrors the "Lint and Format Check" job of rust.yml.
      - id: cargo-fmt
        name: cargo fmt
        entry: cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all --
        language: system
        types: [rust]
        pass_filenames: false

      - id: cargo-clippy
        name: cargo clippy
        entry: cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
        language: system
        types: [rust]
        pass_filenames: false

      # Mirrors the "Lint and Format Check" job of csharp.yml. The solution sets
      # TreatWarningsAsErrors in csharp/Directory.Build.props, so a plain build
      # is already the warning gate.
      - id: dotnet-format
        name: dotnet format
        entry: dotnet format csharp --verify-no-changes
        language: system
        types: [c#]
        pass_filenames: false

      # Mirrors the workflow policy and repository layout guards. These are pure
      # Node with no dependencies, so they are fast enough for every commit.
      - id: workflow-policy
        name: workflow policy and repository layout tests
        entry: node --test .github/scripts/*.test.mjs js/test/*.test.mjs csharp/scripts/*.test.mjs
        language: system
        files: ^(\.github/|js/|csharp/|rust/|\.lycheeignore|README\.md)
        pass_filenames: false

      - id: javascript-quality
        name: JavaScript lint and formatting
        entry: node .github/scripts/check-javascript-quality.mjs
        language: system
        files: \.(js|mjs|cjs|jsx)$
        exclude: ^(dev/log/|docs/case-studies/)
        pass_filenames: false

      - id: secrets
        name: secrets in tracked files including ignored evidence
        entry: node .github/scripts/check-secrets.mjs
        language: system
        pass_filenames: false

      - id: python-quality
        name: Python lint, formatting and CI helper types
        entry: python .github/scripts/check-python-quality.py
        language: python
        additional_dependencies: [ruff==0.17.4, mypy==2.4.1]
        types: [python]
        exclude: ^(dev/log/|docs/case-studies/)
        pass_filenames: false

mv "$logs/main-runs.json.tmp" "$logs/main-runs.json"
{
  jq -r --arg head "$(git rev-parse "origin/$branch")" '.[]|select(.headSha == $head and .status == "completed")|[.databaseId,.conclusion]|@tsv' "$logs/branch-runs.json"
  jq -r --arg base "$(git rev-parse origin/main)" '.[]|select(.headSha == $base and .status == "completed")|[.databaseId,.conclusion]|@tsv' "$logs/main-runs.json"
} | while IFS=$'\t' read -r id conclusion; do
  if [[ -f "$logs/runs/$id.log.gz" || -f "$logs/runs/$id.unavailable.txt" || -f "${logs%/ci-logs}/runs/$id.log.gz" ]]; then
    continue
  fi
  gh run view "$id" --repo "$repo" --json databaseId,name,status,conclusion,createdAt,updatedAt,headSha,url,event,jobs,attempt > "$logs/runs/$id.json.tmp"
  mv "$logs/runs/$id.json.tmp" "$logs/runs/$id.json"
  if gh run view "$id" --repo "$repo" --log 2>"$logs/runs/$id.stderr" | gzip -n > "$logs/runs/$id.log.gz.tmp"; then

  fi
  if [[ "$conclusion" == failure || "$conclusion" == cancelled || "$conclusion" == timed_out ]]; then
    if ! gh run view "$id" --repo "$repo" --log-failed > "$logs/runs/$id.failed.log" 2>"$logs/runs/$id.failed.stderr"; then

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
repo=link-foundation/link-cli
branch=issue-207-ac4b1e2ba1ef
logs=dev/log/issues/207/pulls/208/ci-logs
mkdir -p "$logs"/{reviews,runs}
fields=databaseId,name,status,conclusion,createdAt,updatedAt,headSha,url,event
gh run list --repo "$repo" --branch "$branch" --limit 25 --json "$fields" > "$logs/branch-runs.json.tmp"
mv "$logs/branch-runs.json.tmp" "$logs/branch-runs.json"
gh run list --repo "$repo" --branch main --event push --limit 25 --json "$fields" > "$logs/main-runs.json.tmp"
mv "$logs/main-runs.json.tmp" "$logs/main-runs.json"
{
  jq -r --arg head "$(git rev-parse "origin/$branch")" '.[]|select(.headSha == $head and .status == "completed")|[.databaseId,.conclusion]|@tsv' "$logs/branch-runs.json"
  jq -r --arg base "$(git rev-parse origin/main)" '.[]|select(.headSha == $base and .status == "completed")|[.databaseId,.conclusion]|@tsv' "$logs/main-runs.json"
} | while IFS=$'\t' read -r id conclusion; do
  if [[ -f "$logs/runs/$id.log.gz" || -f "$logs/runs/$id.unavailable.txt" || -f "${logs%/ci-logs}/runs/$id.log.gz" ]]; then
    continue
  fi
  gh run view "$id" --repo "$repo" --json databaseId,name,status,conclusion,createdAt,updatedAt,headSha,url,event,jobs,attempt > "$logs/runs/$id.json.tmp"
  mv "$logs/runs/$id.json.tmp" "$logs/runs/$id.json"
  if gh run view "$id" --repo "$repo" --log 2>"$logs/runs/$id.stderr" | gzip -n > "$logs/runs/$id.log.gz.tmp"; then
    mv "$logs/runs/$id.log.gz.tmp" "$logs/runs/$id.log.gz"
    rm -f "$logs/runs/$id.stderr"
  else
    rm -f "$logs/runs/$id.log.gz.tmp"
    if [[ "$conclusion" == skipped ]] && rg -q 'log not found|no logs' "$logs/runs/$id.stderr"; then
      mv "$logs/runs/$id.stderr" "$logs/runs/$id.unavailable.txt"
    fi
  fi
  if [[ "$conclusion" == failure || "$conclusion" == cancelled || "$conclusion" == timed_out ]]; then
    if ! gh run view "$id" --repo "$repo" --log-failed > "$logs/runs/$id.failed.log" 2>"$logs/runs/$id.failed.stderr"; then
      continue
    fi
    rm -f "$logs/runs/$id.failed.stderr"
  fi
  jq -r '[.databaseId,.name,.conclusion]|@tsv' "$logs/runs/$id.json"
done

text(await tools.apply_patch(`*** Begin Patch
*** Update File: docs/case-studies/issue-207/README.md
@@
 | 22:11 | All 14 workflows passed on the first PR revision, \`b2c74235\`. Windows Rust passed the full suite, golden receipt check and native LSM example runs within its existing budget. [Rust pipeline](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/actions/runs/46069793342) |
+| 22:20 | While testing \`e4ababbb\`, Windows IPC exited after JavaScript received \`EPERM\` deleting a mapped ring during stream teardown. The same matrix passed on \`b2c74235\` and the latest main revision. [Failed job](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/actions/runs/46075606690/job/140762688754) |
@@
 | Resolve actionable CI warnings | Move Rust’s local transaction tests to a sibling module and centralize C# import option parsing in the existing I/O class. Both files are below the existing 900-line warning threshold. Parity fingerprints were updated with structural-change acknowledgements. Release fragments trigger the normal package release paths. |
+| Keep cross-language IPC checks reliable | Windows may deny deletion while a native peer still maps a ring region. JavaScript now leaves that deletion for the last endpoint to close, matching the native implementations and the protocol. Early deletion, other filesystem errors and the original handshake rejection are covered by the focused tests. The JS client version advances to \`0.5.1\`. |
@@
 - **Election observation.** The etcd v3 maintenance endpoint already supplies member, leader and term. Polling it while the original process is stopped provides direct evidence without a new client dependency or an arbitrary election sleep. [etcd maintenance API](https://etcd.io/docs/v3.6/dev-guide/api_reference_v3/#service-maintenance-etcdserveretcdserverpb-rpc-proto)
+- **Windows ring ownership.** The JS descriptor closes first in the failed interop conversation, and the native peer can retain its mapped view until it sees the hangup. Both native implementations already close their views before attempting removal, so the JS client can return from teardown on Windows sharing errors and let that peer remove the file. The alternative of fixed-delay retries would keep the JS stream open and still depend on when the peer releases its view. The existing \`CLINK_IPC_TRACE=1\` toggle records when deletion falls to the peer. [IPC protocol](../../protocol/ipc-transports-v1.md#rendezvous-directory) · [Windows DeleteFileW](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fileapi/nf-fileapi-deletefilew#remarks)
*** End Patch`));

item.aggregated_output:
Fixes #207

## Changes

- Keep read-only checks for each default-branch revision and independent dispatch. Replace only superseded PR synchronization checks. Queue repository release writers so a later publish cannot displace a pending one.
- Remove the generated root `.gitkeep`. Preserve required status checks, language stage order, and golden fixture receipts.
- Verify the replacement etcd leader while the original member is paused. After it rejoins, verify convergence, refusal of the stale transaction, and a linearizable read through the resumed member. Set `ETCD_TEST_VERBOSE=1` or dispatch JS Client CI with **Record etcd election status and member debug logs** to capture election evidence.
- Fix Windows `mmap` and `file` ring teardown. A peer can still hold the mapping after JavaScript closes its descriptor. Both endpoints attempt removal after closing their regions, and JavaScript defers the sharing error to the peer. Bump the JS client to `0.5.1`.
- Validate both npm tarballs and their size against the JS template’s budget on pull requests and checks-only dispatches. Main publishing requires a successful trusted-publisher preflight. A separate read-only job downloads the exact published version anonymously. Registry diagnostics distinguish package setup from a lookup outage.
- Cover shared stage inputs and integration examples in JS package triggers. Enforce a 30-minute workflow job timeout ceiling with documented caps for longer suites and release jobs. Resolve the Rust and C# source-size warnings and include release fragments.

## Reproduce and verify

- Draft #208 at `26852bd` fails `node --test js/test/repositoryLayout.test.mjs`. This test passes after removal of the placeholder.
- The original run reproduces the etcd failure. JS Client CI runs the real cluster in both journal modes. Run `node --test experiments/issue-138/etcd-harness.test.mjs` for the focused election checks. [Original failure](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/actions/runs/46062568123)
- Windows IPC reproduced the mapped-file `EPERM`. Run `node --test --test-name-pattern='Windows ring cleanup' js/client/test/ipc-ring.test.mjs` to exercise shutdown, a handshake rejection and other I/O errors. The unchanged hosted IPC matrix also runs cross-language mmap and file conversations on Windows. [Original failure](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/actions/runs/46075606690/job/140762688754)
- Overlapping `main` revisions cancelled conformance and Rust tests. Run the CI governance and workflow policy tests in `.github/scripts` to exercise the policy. [Client cancellation](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/actions/runs/46059980457) · [Rust cancellation](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/actions/runs/46059980682)
- Hosted etcd passed the revised scenario in both journal modes. The anonymous package check downloaded `@link-foundation/link-cli-client@0.5.0` and reproduced npm HTTP 404 for `@link-foundation/link-cli-server@0.1.1`. [Hosted conformance](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/actions/runs/46069793278/job/140744356887)
- Run `npm --prefix js run lint`, `npm --prefix js run test:js`, `node parity/check-parity.mjs --base origin/main`, and `npm pack --dry-run --json | node ../../.github/scripts/check-npm-tarball-size.mjs` from each npm package directory.
- This environment has no installed pre-commit hooks. The relevant checks were run manually, including workflow policy, JavaScript and Python quality, secrets, Rust formatting and lint, .NET formatting on the CI SDK, Actionlint and zizmor.

## Registry setup still needed

The npm server package is absent from the public registry, and its OIDC exchange returns HTTP 404. An npm scope maintainer needs to publish the first public version or make an existing private package public, configure GitHub trusted publishing for `link-foundation/link-cli` and `js-server.yml`, and run JS server CI on `main` with **Verify npm trusted publishing** enabled before retrying the main workflow. The PR’s tarball and code checks run independently. The real publishing criterion remains open until the maintainer steps and main verification succeed. [Failed preflight](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/actions/runs/46067149214)

## Evidence and upstream reports

- [Investigation, timeline and requirements](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/blob/issue-207-ac4b1e2ba1ef/docs/case-studies/issue-207/README.md)
- [Run logs, template file comparison and local verification](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/blob/issue-207-ac4b1e2ba1ef/dev/log/issues/207/pulls/208/README.md)

name: Security

# Mirrors the security workflow shared by the C#, Rust and JS
# ai-driven-development-pipeline templates, merged into a single file because
# this repository ships all three languages (issue #96).

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 6 * * 1'
  workflow_dispatch:

# Least-privilege default; jobs escalate individually when needed.
permissions:
  contents: read

# Provide Git config to actions/checkout itself; checkout runs git init before
# any workflow step can configure Git, which otherwise prints the
# default-branch hint into every log.
env:
  GIT_CONFIG_COUNT: '1'
  GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0: ini…nch
  GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0: main

jobs:
  # === STAGE GATE (issue #111) ===
  # Jobs that install Rust or .NET wait for the JavaScript stage (lint,
  # `npm run test:js`, parity check) of the same commit; a failed, cancelled
  # or skipped stage leaves them skipped.
  javascript:
    name: javascript
    uses: ./.github/workflows/javascript-stage.yml

  codeql:
    name: CodeQL (${{ matrix.language }})
    needs: [javascript]
    # Cached overlay-base SARIF retains extraction diagnostics from the base
    # even after the PR repairs the source (confirmed in run 42133108866).
    # A full database makes the completeness gate describe this checkout.
    env:
      CODEQL_OVERLAY_DATABASE_MODE: none
      # The compare API truncates at 300 files and warns on evidence-heavy PRs.
      # Run the complete queries directly, alongside the full extraction above.
      CODEQL_ACTION_DIFF_INFORMED_QUERIES: 'false'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 30
    concurrency:
      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.action == 'synchronize' && github.ref || github.event_name == 'push' && github.sha || github.run_id }}-codeql-${{ matrix.language }}
      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.action == 'synchronize' }}
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: read
      security-events: write
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      # build-mode has to be declared per language. Leaving it unset made every
      # run log "Cannot build an overlay database because build-mode is set to
      # 'undefined'" and fall back to a full database, and drove the standalone
      # autobuild step, whose inputs the action now reports as DEPRECATED
      # (issue #96). C# used `autobuild`, which still logged "Cannot build an
      # overlay-base database because build-mode is set to "autobuild" instead
      # of "none"" on every run (issue #134); buildless extraction is supported
      # for C#, so every language is now analysed from source.
      matrix:
        include:
          - language: csharp
            build-mode: none
          - language: rust
            build-mode: none
          - language: javascript-typescript
            build-mode: none
          - language: python
            build-mode: none
          - language: actions
            build-mode: none
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      # Buildless C# extraction still restores NuGet packages to resolve
      # dependency types, so the SDK stays.
      - name: Setup .NET
        if: matrix.language == 'csharp'
        uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v6
        with:
          dotnet-version: '10.0.403' # Exact version uses the public builds feed; channel redirect returns HTTP 409.

      # With build-mode set here the action builds the database itself, so the
      # deprecated github/codeql-action/autobuild step is no longer needed.
      - name: Initialize CodeQL
        uses: github/codeql-action/init@v4
        with:
          languages: ${{ matrix.language }}
          build-mode: ${{ matrix.build-mode }}
          config-file: ./.github/codeql/codeql-config.yml
          # Opt in when an upload/extraction fails without useful diagnostics.
          debug: ${{ vars.CI_VERBOSE == 'true' }}

      - name: Analyze
        uses: github/codeql-action/analyze@v4
        with:
          output: codeql-results

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '26.x'

      - name: Require complete analysis without unresolved findings
        run: node .github/scripts/check-codeql-results.mjs codeql-results

      - name: Preserve SARIF for investigation
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: codeql-${{ matrix.language }}
          path: codeql-results/**/*.sarif
          if-no-files-found: error

  dependency-review:
    name: Dependency Review
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 10
    concurrency:
      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.action == 'synchronize' && github.ref || github.event_name == 'push' && github.sha || github.run_id }}-dependency-review
      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.action == 'synchronize' }}
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Review dependency changes
        uses: actions/dependency-review-action@v5
        with:
          fail-on-severity: high
          comment-summary-in-pr: on-failure

  cargo-audit:
    name: Cargo audit (${{ matrix.manifest }})
    needs: [javascript]
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 10
    concurrency:
      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.action == 'synchronize' && github.ref || github.event_name == 'push' && github.sha || github.run_id }}-cargo-audit-${{ matrix.manifest }}
      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.action == 'synchronize' }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        manifest: [rust, rust/wasm, docs/case-studies/issue-100/evidence/external-range/rust]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@073e1fd0bc889c9aee68dbaaa927cde1b5653a83 # v2.90.11
        with:
          tool: cargo-audit@0.23.0

      # `unmaintained`, `unsound` and `yanked` advisories are warnings, and a
      # warning does not move `cargo audit`'s exit status: it prints
      # "warning: N allowed warnings found" and exits 0, so the job passed while
      # showing findings (issue #134). Ported from the
      # rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template.
      - name: Audit committed Cargo.lock
        env:
          MANIFEST: ${{ matrix.manifest }}
        run: cargo audit --file "$MANIFEST/Cargo.lock" --deny warnings

  npm-audit:
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        directory: [js, js/client, js/server]
    name: Audit npm lock (${{ matrix.directory }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 10
    concurrency:
      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.action == 'synchronize' && github.ref || github.event_name == 'push' && github.sha || github.run_id }}-npm-audit-${{ matrix.directory }}
      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.action == 'synchronize' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '26.x'

      - name: Audit current lock
        working-directory: ${{ matrix.directory }}
        run: npm audit --package-lock-only --audit-level=high

  nuget-audit:
    name: Audit every NuGet dependency graph
    needs: [javascript]
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 15
    concurrency:
      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.action == 'synchronize' && github.ref || github.event_name == 'push' && github.sha || github.run_id }}-nuget-audit
      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.action == 'synchronize' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v6
        with:
          dotnet-version: '10.0.403' # Exact version uses the public builds feed; channel redirect returns HTTP 409.
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '26.x'
      - name: Audit direct and transitive packages and validate the complete result
        run: node .github/scripts/audit-nuget-dependencies.mjs
      - name: Preserve dependency graphs and diagnostics
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: nuget-audit
          path: artifacts/security
          if-no-files-found: error

  python-audit:
    name: Audit resolved Python CI tools
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 10
    concurrency:
      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.action == 'synchronize' && github.ref || github.event_name == 'push' && github.sha || github.run_id }}-python-audit
      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.action == 'synchronize' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with:
          python-version: '3.14'
      - name: Audit pinned tools and their resolved dependencies
        run: pipx run pip-audit==2.10.1 --strict --requirement .github/scripts/requirements-quality.txt

  # === COMMITTED SECRETS ===
  # CodeQL and the audit jobs look at code and dependencies; nothing looked at
  # the literal contents of the tree. This repository commits CI evidence under
  # dev/log, which is exactly where a token pasted from a workflow log would end
  # up unnoticed (issue #96). Ported from the pipeline templates' secrets-scan
  # job. Git inventories tracked files, including force-added logs/experiments;
  # build-output ignores must never hide committed evidence from this scan.
  secrets-scan:
    name: Scan for committed secrets
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 10
    concurrency:
      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.action == 'synchronize' && github.ref || github.event_name == 'push' && github.sha || github.run_id }}-secrets-scan
      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.action == 'synchronize' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '26.x'

      - name: Install locked secret scanner
        run: npm ci --prefix js --ignore-scripts
      - name: Run secretlint on every tracked file
        run: node .github/scripts/check-secrets.mjs
      - name: Verify ignored-log regression
        run: node experiments/issue-165/reproduce-ignored-secret.mjs

  pipeline-status:
    name: Pipeline Status (security)
    needs:
      - javascript
      - codeql
      - dependency-review
      - cargo-audit
      - npm-audit
      - nuget-audit
      - python-audit
      - secrets-scan
    if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 5
    concurrency:
      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.action == 'synchronize' && github.ref || github.event_name == 'push' && github.sha || github.run_id }}-pipeline-status
      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.action == 'synchronize' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '26.x'
      - name: Check every prerequisite
        working-directory: .
        env:
          NEEDS_JSON: ${{ toJSON(needs) }}
        run: node .github/scripts/pipeline-status.mjs

name: Security

# Mirrors the security workflow shared by the C#, Rust and JS
# ai-driven-development-pipeline templates, merged into a single file because
# this repository ships all three languages (issue #96).

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 6 * * 1'
  workflow_dispatch:

# Least-privilege default; jobs escalate individually when needed.
permissions:
  contents: read

# Provide Git config to actions/checkout itself; checkout runs git init before
# any workflow step can configure Git, which otherwise prints the
# default-branch hint into every log.
env:
  GIT_CONFIG_COUNT: '1'
  GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0: ini…nch
  GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0: main

jobs:
  # === STAGE GATE (issue #111) ===
  # Jobs that install Rust or .NET wait for the JavaScript stage (lint,
  # `npm run test:js`, parity check) of the same commit; a failed, cancelled
  # or skipped stage leaves them skipped.
  javascript:
    name: javascript
    uses: ./.github/workflows/javascript-stage.yml

  codeql:
    name: CodeQL (${{ matrix.language }})
    needs: [javascript]
    # Cached overlay-base SARIF retains extraction diagnostics from the base
    # even after the PR repairs the source (confirmed in run 42133108866).
    # A full database makes the completeness gate describe this checkout.
    env:
      CODEQL_OVERLAY_DATABASE_MODE: none
      # The compare API truncates at 300 files and warns on evidence-heavy PRs.
      # Run the complete queries directly, alongside the full extraction above.
      CODEQL_ACTION_DIFF_INFORMED_QUERIES: 'false'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 30
    concurrency:
      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.action == 'synchronize' && github.ref || github.event_name == 'push' && github.sha || github.run_id }}-codeql-${{ matrix.language }}
      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.action == 'synchronize' }}
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: read
      security-events: write
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      # build-mode has to be declared per language. Leaving it unset made every
      # run log "Cannot build an overlay database because build-mode is set to
      # 'undefined'" and fall back to a full database, and drove the standalone
      # autobuild step, whose inputs the action now reports as DEPRECATED
      # (issue #96). C# used `autobuild`, which still logged "Cannot build an
      # overlay-base database because build-mode is set to "autobuild" instead
      # of "none"" on every run (issue #134); buildless extraction is supported
      # for C#, so every language is now analysed from source.
      matrix:
        include:
          - language: csharp
            build-mode: none
          - language: rust
            build-mode: none
          - language: javascript-typescript
            build-mode: none
          - language: python
            build-mode: none
          - language: actions
            build-mode: none
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      # Buildless C# extraction still restores NuGet packages to resolve
      # dependency types, so the SDK stays.
      - name: Setup .NET
        if: matrix.language == 'csharp'
        uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v6
        with:
          dotnet-version: '10.0.403' # Exact version uses the public builds feed; channel redirect returns HTTP 409.

      # With build-mode set here the action builds the database itself, so the
      # deprecated github/codeql-action/autobuild step is no longer needed.
      - name: Initialize CodeQL
        uses: github/codeql-action/init@v4
        with:
          languages: ${{ matrix.language }}
          build-mode: ${{ matrix.build-mode }}
          config-file: ./.github/codeql/codeql-config.yml
          # Opt in when an upload/extraction fails without useful diagnostics.
          debug: ${{ vars.CI_VERBOSE == 'true' }}

      - name: Analyze
        uses: github/codeql-action/analyze@v4
        with:
          output: codeql-results

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '26.x'

      - name: Require complete analysis without unresolved findings
        run: node .github/scripts/check-codeql-results.mjs codeql-results

      - name: Preserve SARIF for investigation
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: codeql-${{ matrix.language }}
          path: codeql-results/**/*.sarif
          if-no-files-found: error

  dependency-review:
    name: Dependency Review
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 10
    concurrency:
      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.action == 'synchronize' && github.ref || github.event_name == 'push' && github.sha || github.run_id }}-dependency-review
      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.action == 'synchronize' }}
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Review dependency changes
        uses: actions/dependency-review-action@v5
        with:
          fail-on-severity: high
          comment-summary-in-pr: on-failure

  cargo-audit:
    name: Cargo audit (${{ matrix.manifest }})
    needs: [javascript]
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 10
    concurrency:
      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.action == 'synchronize' && github.ref || github.event_name == 'push' && github.sha || github.run_id }}-cargo-audit-${{ matrix.manifest }}
      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.action == 'synchronize' }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        manifest: [rust, rust/wasm, docs/case-studies/issue-100/evidence/external-range/rust]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@073e1fd0bc889c9aee68dbaaa927cde1b5653a83 # v2.90.11
        with:
          tool: cargo-audit@0.23.0

      # `unmaintained`, `unsound` and `yanked` advisories are warnings, and a
      # warning does not move `cargo audit`'s exit status: it prints
      # "warning: N allowed warnings found" and exits 0, so the job passed while
      # showing findings (issue #134). Ported from the
      # rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template.
      - name: Audit committed Cargo.lock
        env:
          MANIFEST: ${{ matrix.manifest }}
        run: cargo audit --file "$MANIFEST/Cargo.lock" --deny warnings

  npm-audit:
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        directory: [js, js/client, js/server]
    name: Audit npm lock (${{ matrix.directory }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 10
    concurrency:
      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.action == 'synchronize' && github.ref || github.event_name == 'push' && github.sha || github.run_id }}-npm-audit-${{ matrix.directory }}
      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.action == 'synchronize' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '26.x'

      - name: Audit current lock
        working-directory: ${{ matrix.directory }}
        run: npm audit --package-lock-only --audit-level=high

  nuget-audit:
    name: Audit every NuGet dependency graph
    needs: [javascript]
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 15
    concurrency:
      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.action == 'synchronize' && github.ref || github.event_name == 'push' && github.sha || github.run_id }}-nuget-audit
      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.action == 'synchronize' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v6
        with:
          dotnet-version: '10.0.403' # Exact version uses the public builds feed; channel redirect returns HTTP 409.
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '26.x'
      - name: Audit direct and transitive packages and validate the complete result
        run: node .github/scripts/audit-nuget-dependencies.mjs
      - name: Preserve dependency graphs and diagnostics
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: nuget-audit
          path: artifacts/security
          if-no-files-found: error

  python-audit:
    name: Audit resolved Python CI tools
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 10
    concurrency:
      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.action == 'synchronize' && github.ref || github.event_name == 'push' && github.sha || github.run_id }}-python-audit
      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.action == 'synchronize' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with:
          python-version: '3.14'
      - name: Audit pinned tools and their resolved dependencies
        run: pipx run pip-audit==2.10.1 --strict --requirement .github/scripts/requirements-quality.txt

  # === COMMITTED SECRETS ===
  # CodeQL and the audit jobs look at code and dependencies; nothing looked at
  # the literal contents of the tree. This repository commits CI evidence under
  # dev/log, which is exactly where a token pasted from a workflow log would end
  # up unnoticed (issue #96). Ported from the pipeline templates' secrets-scan
  # job. Git inventories tracked files, including force-added logs/experiments;
  # build-output ignores must never hide committed evidence from this scan.
  secrets-scan:
    name: Scan for committed secrets
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 10
    concurrency:
      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.action == 'synchronize' && github.ref || github.event_name == 'push' && github.sha || github.run_id }}-secrets-scan
      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.action == 'synchronize' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '26.x'

      - name: Install locked secret scanner
        run: npm ci --prefix js --ignore-scripts
      - name: Run secretlint on every tracked file
        run: node .github/scripts/check-secrets.mjs
      - name: Verify ignored-log regression
        run: node experiments/issue-165/reproduce-ignored-secret.mjs

  pipeline-status:
    name: Pipeline Status (security)
    needs:
      - javascript
      - codeql
      - dependency-review
      - cargo-audit
      - npm-audit
      - nuget-audit
      - python-audit
      - secrets-scan
    if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 5
    concurrency:
      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.action == 'synchronize' && github.ref || github.event_name == 'push' && github.sha || github.run_id }}-pipeline-status
      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.action == 'synchronize' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '26.x'
      - name: Check every prerequisite
        working-directory: .
        env:
          NEEDS_JSON: ${{ toJSON(needs) }}
        run: node .github/scripts/pipeline-status.mjs
